packs.title: Quick & Easy 10-Second Brain Warm-Up
packs.subtitle: 100% Easy instant-solve tasks across Math, Logic, Science, Chess & Words for fast unlocks
packs.author: Kmito Fast-Flow Lab

questions.question: What is 15 + 12?
questions.explanation: 15 + 10 = 25, plus 2 more equals 27!
questions.hintText: Split 12 into 10 and 2, then add them one by one.

questions.question: If today is Tuesday, what day of the week will it be tomorrow?
questions.explanation: The day directly after Tuesday is Wednesday.
questions.hintText: Monday, Tuesday, ...?

questions.question: At what temperature (in °C) does liquid water boil into steam at sea level?
questions.explanation: Water freezes at 0 °C and boils at 100 °C at standard atmospheric pressure.
questions.hintText: Think of a bubbling kettle. It is much hotter than a warm bath.

questions.question: White to move: Find the winning move to capture Black's undefended piece!
questions.explanation: 1. Rxd5 wins Black's Queen for free along the open d-file!
questions.hintText: Look along the open file: your Rook can take a piece nobody protects.

questions.question: Which word means the SAME as 'HAPPY'?
questions.explanation: 'Joyful' means full of happiness and delight.
questions.hintText: Think about how you feel on your birthday.

questions.question: What number does print(5 + 5) show on the screen?
questions.explanation: 5 + 5 adds the two numbers together and prints 10.
questions.hintText: The computer adds first, then shows the result.

questions.question: What is 25 + 35?
questions.hintText: Add the tens first, then the ones.

questions.question: 2, 4, 8, 16, ... What comes next?
questions.explanation: Each number is double the one before: 16 x 2 = 32.
questions.hintText: Double each number.

questions.question: What is the brightest star seen from Earth during the day?
questions.explanation: The Sun is a star, and it is so close to Earth that it outshines every other star.
questions.hintText: It lights up our day!

questions.question: What is a synonym for 'tiny'?
questions.explanation: Tiny means very small.
questions.hintText: Think of a tiny insect.

questions.question: Which piece can move backward, forward, and sideways any number of squares?
questions.explanation: The Rook moves horizontally and vertically any distance.
questions.hintText: It goes in straight lines and never diagonally.

questions.question: In Python, len() counts the letters in a word. What is len('Cat')?
questions.explanation: 'Cat' has 3 characters: C, a, t.
questions.hintText: Count the letters in Cat.

questions.question: What is 12 x 5?
questions.hintText: Split 12 into 10 and 2, multiply each by 5, then add.

questions.question: There are 3 apples on a table and you take 2 of them. How many apples do you have now?
questions.explanation: You took 2 apples, so you have 2 apples!
questions.hintText: Look at the apples in YOUR hands, not on the table.

questions.question: What do we call the energy a car has because it is moving?
questions.explanation: Anything that moves has movement energy. Scientists call it kinetic energy.
questions.hintText: The faster the car goes, the more of this energy it has.

questions.question: What is the opposite of 'Victory'?
questions.explanation: Defeat is the opposite of victory.
questions.hintText: Think of how the losing team feels at the end of the game.

questions.question: What is 48 / 6?
questions.hintText: Count by 6s up to 48.

questions.question: Which of these can a pawn promote to when it reaches the 8th rank?
questions.explanation: A pawn can promote to a Queen, Rook, Bishop, or Knight.
questions.hintText: Promotion is a reward: your pawn becomes a strong piece.

questions.question: Which symbol is used for comments in Python?
questions.explanation: # denotes a single-line comment in Python.
questions.hintText: Look for the sign shaped like a tic-tac-toe grid.

questions.question: If you face North and turn 90 degrees clockwise, which way do you face?
questions.explanation: Turning clockwise from North points to East.
questions.hintText: Clockwise is to the right, like the hands of a clock.

questions.question: Can sound travel through empty space, where there is no air?
questions.optionsString: Yes|No|Only in zero gravity|Faster than in air
questions.explanation: Sound needs something to shake, like air, water or a wall. Empty space has nothing to shake, so it stays silent.
questions.hintText: Sound is a shaking that passes from one particle to the next.

questions.question: What is 9 squared (9 x 9)?
questions.explanation: 9 x 10 = 90, and one 9 less is 90 - 9 = 81.
questions.hintText: Try 9 x 10 first, then take away one 9.

questions.question: Which of these is a compound word?
questions.explanation: Sun + light = Sunlight.
questions.hintText: Like football = foot + ball. Which word splits into two words?

questions.question: What is it called when the King is attacked and cannot escape?
questions.explanation: Checkmate ends the game with a win for the attacker.
questions.hintText: The ultimate goal in chess.

questions.question: In code, what do we call a row of items kept in order?
questions.explanation: A list keeps items in order, one after another. Some coding languages call it an array.
questions.hintText: Think of a row of numbered boxes, one item in each.

questions.question: A square has sides of 5 cm. What is its perimeter?
questions.explanation: Perimeter = 4 x 5 cm = 20 cm.
questions.hintText: Add all 4 sides.

questions.question: Which one is NOT a mammal?
questions.explanation: An eagle is a bird, while dolphins and whales are mammals.
questions.hintText: Mammals feed milk to their babies. Which one doesn't?

questions.question: How does heat travel from the Sun to Earth across space?
questions.explanation: The Sun's heat travels as rays, like its light. This is called radiation, and it can cross empty space.
questions.hintText: Space is empty, so nothing can carry the heat. Think of light.

questions.question: Which word is spelled correctly?
questions.explanation: 'Definitely' is the correct spelling.
questions.hintText: It begins like the word 'define'.

questions.question: What is half of 84?
questions.explanation: Half of 80 is 40, and half of 4 is 2. 40 + 2 = 42.
questions.hintText: Halve 80 first, then halve 4, and add the two parts.

questions.question: Which two pieces participate in castling?
questions.optionsString: King and Queen|King and Rook|Bishop and Knight|Rook and Pawn
questions.explanation: Castling is a special move involving King and Rook.
questions.hintText: The other piece is the one standing in the corner of the board.

questions.question: What does the % (modulo) operator calculate?
questions.explanation: Modulo returns the remainder (e.g. 7 % 3 = 1).
questions.hintText: Share 10 sweets between 3 kids. Look at the sweets left over.

questions.question: How many seconds are in 3 minutes?
questions.explanation: 3 x 60 = 180 seconds.
questions.hintText: 60 seconds in 1 minute.

questions.question: What is 20 - 7?
questions.explanation: 10 - 7 = 3, and with the other ten that makes 13.
questions.hintText: Take 7 away from 10 first, then add the other ten.

questions.question: What is 6 x 3?
questions.hintText: Add 6 three times.

questions.question: How many corners does a square have?
questions.explanation: A square has 4 corners and 4 sides of the same length.
questions.hintText: Draw one in the air and count the corners.

questions.question: Which of these numbers is even?
questions.explanation: Even numbers can be split into two equal groups. 12 = 6 + 6, so 12 is even.
questions.hintText: Even numbers end in 0, 2, 4, 6 or 8.

questions.question: What is double 8?
questions.explanation: Double means two times. 8 + 8 = 16.
questions.hintText: Double means: add the number to itself.

questions.question: How many centimeters are in 1 meter?
questions.explanation: 1 meter is the same as 100 centimeters. A big step is about 1 meter long.
questions.hintText: A school ruler is 30 cm long. A meter is a bit longer than 3 rulers.

questions.question: Which of these numbers is the biggest?
questions.explanation: Look at the tens first. 93 has 9 tens, more than any other number here.
questions.hintText: Compare the first digit of each number.

questions.question: Which number comes just before 50?
questions.explanation: Counting goes 48, 49, 50. So 49 comes just before 50.
questions.hintText: Count back one step.

questions.question: Mia has 6 stickers and gets 5 more. How many stickers does she have now?
questions.explanation: 6 + 5 = 11. Tip: 6 + 4 = 10, and 1 more makes 11.
questions.hintText: Add the new stickers to the ones she already had.

questions.question: How many minutes are in one hour?
questions.explanation: One hour has 60 minutes. Half an hour has 30 minutes.
questions.hintText: In this time the long hand goes once around the whole clock face.

questions.question: 7 + ? = 10. Which number is missing?
questions.explanation: 7 + 3 = 10. Count on from 7: 8, 9, 10. That is 3 steps.
questions.hintText: Count on from 7 until you reach 10.

questions.question: A pizza is cut into 4 equal pieces. What is one piece called?
questions.explanation: 4 equal pieces are 4 quarters. One piece is one quarter of the pizza.
questions.hintText: A clock uses the same word for 15 minutes.

questions.question: 5, 10, 15, 20, ... What comes next?
questions.explanation: The numbers go up by 5 each time. 20 + 5 = 25.
questions.hintText: How big is the jump from one number to the next?

questions.question: Which one does not belong with the others?
questions.explanation: Apple, banana and pear are fruits. A carrot is a vegetable.
questions.hintText: Three of them are sweet fruits. One grows under the ground.

questions.question: Tom is taller than Ben. Ben is taller than Sam. Who is the shortest?
questions.explanation: From tallest to shortest: Tom, Ben, Sam. So Sam is the shortest.
questions.hintText: Line the three boys up from tallest to smallest.

questions.question: Which month comes right after March?
questions.explanation: The months go January, February, March, April. April comes right after March.
questions.hintText: Say the months in order, starting with January.

questions.question: Red, blue, red, blue, red, ... Which color comes next?
questions.explanation: The colors take turns: red, then blue. After red comes blue.
questions.hintText: The pattern has two colors that take turns.

questions.question: Anna has one sister and one brother. How many children are in the family?
questions.explanation: Anna, her sister and her brother make 3 children. Do not forget to count Anna!
questions.hintText: Who else is a child in this family, besides the sister and the brother?

questions.question: What is heavier, 1 kilogram of feathers or 1 kilogram of stones?
questions.optionsString: The stones|The feathers|They weigh the same|Nobody can tell
questions.explanation: Both weigh 1 kilogram, so they weigh the same. You just need many more feathers!
questions.hintText: Read the two weights again before you choose.

questions.question: A glove goes on a hand. A sock goes on a ...?
questions.explanation: A glove covers a hand, and a sock covers a foot.
questions.hintText: Think about what you put on before your shoes.

questions.question: All birds in the park are white. Pip is a bird in the park. What color is Pip?
questions.explanation: Every bird in the park is white. Pip is one of them, so Pip is white.
questions.hintText: Pip is one of the park birds. What is true for all of them?

questions.question: Which day comes between Wednesday and Friday?
questions.explanation: The days go Wednesday, Thursday, Friday. Thursday is in the middle.
questions.hintText: Say the days of the week in order.

questions.question: Two dogs meet in the park. How many legs do they have together?
questions.explanation: One dog has 4 legs. Two dogs have 4 + 4 = 8 legs.
questions.hintText: Count the legs of one dog first.

questions.question: What does a green plant need to make its food?
questions.explanation: Plants use sunlight, water and air to make their own food in their leaves.
questions.hintText: Plants on a dark shelf grow badly. What are they missing?

questions.question: What does ice turn into when it melts?
questions.explanation: Ice is frozen water. When it gets warm, it melts back into liquid water.
questions.hintText: Think of an ice cube left in a glass on a warm day.

questions.question: How many legs does a spider have?
questions.explanation: A spider has 8 legs. Insects like ants and bees have only 6.
questions.hintText: Spiders are not insects: they have more legs than an ant.

questions.question: Which planet do we live on?
questions.explanation: We live on Earth. It is the third planet from the Sun.
questions.hintText: It is the planet under your feet right now.

questions.question: What pulls a ball back down after you throw it up?
questions.explanation: Gravity is the pull of the Earth. It brings everything back down to the ground.
questions.hintText: The Earth pulls on everything, even on you.

questions.question: What does a caterpillar grow into?
questions.explanation: A caterpillar eats a lot and then rests inside a hard case. It comes out as a butterfly or a moth.
questions.hintText: After a long rest it comes out with colorful wings.

questions.question: Which of these will a magnet pull towards itself?
questions.optionsString: A wooden spoon|A plastic cup|An iron nail|A paper sheet
questions.explanation: Magnets pull things made of iron. Wood, plastic and paper are not pulled.
questions.hintText: Magnets only pull some metals.

questions.question: Which part of your body pumps blood?
questions.explanation: Your heart is a strong muscle. It pumps blood around your whole body.
questions.hintText: You can feel it beating in your chest after you run.

questions.question: Which of these is a liquid?
questions.explanation: A liquid flows and takes the shape of its cup. Milk does that. Stone, wood and ice are solid.
questions.hintText: A liquid can be poured from one cup into another.

questions.question: What do bees make from the nectar of flowers?
questions.explanation: Bees collect sweet nectar from flowers and turn it into honey in their hive.
questions.hintText: It is sweet, golden and sticky.

questions.question: What do we call water drops that fall from clouds?
questions.explanation: Clouds are made of tiny water drops. When the drops get big and heavy, they fall as rain.
questions.hintText: You may need an umbrella when it falls.

questions.question: How many squares does a chessboard have?
questions.explanation: A chessboard has 8 rows of 8 squares. 8 x 8 = 64.
questions.hintText: Count the squares along one side, then think of the rows.

questions.question: Which chess piece can jump over other pieces?
questions.explanation: The knight moves in an L-shape. It is the only piece that can jump over others.
questions.hintText: It looks like a horse.

questions.question: Which chess piece moves only diagonally?
questions.explanation: The bishop moves only along diagonals. That is why it always stays on squares of one color.
questions.hintText: This piece stays on the same color of squares for the whole game.

questions.question: How many pawns does each player have at the start of a chess game?
questions.explanation: Each player starts with 8 pawns. They fill one whole row in front of the other pieces.
questions.hintText: The pawns fill one whole row of the board.

questions.question: Your move attacks the other king, but it can still escape. What is this called?
questions.explanation: An attack on the king is called check. If the king cannot escape, it is checkmate.
questions.hintText: Players often say this short word out loud.

questions.question: How many squares can a king move in one normal move?
questions.explanation: The king moves just 1 square at a time, but in any direction.
questions.hintText: The king is important but slow.

questions.question: On its very first move, how many squares forward can a pawn go at most?
questions.explanation: From its starting square a pawn may go 1 or 2 squares forward. After that, only 1.
questions.hintText: A pawn gets a small head start on its first move.

questions.question: Where do the rooks stand at the start of a chess game?
questions.optionsString: In the middle|In the corners|Next to the king|Next to the queen
questions.explanation: Each player has 2 rooks. They start in the corners of the board.
questions.hintText: Rooks look like castle towers. Where do towers stand on a castle wall?

questions.question: White to move: The Black king is stuck behind its own pawns. Find checkmate in 1 move!
questions.explanation: 1. Re8# is checkmate! The rook attacks the king along the top row, and Black's own pawns block the way out.
questions.hintText: Your rook can reach the top row in one move.

questions.question: White to move: Your king already guards the squares next to Black's king. Find checkmate in 1 move!
questions.explanation: 1. Qh8# is checkmate! The queen attacks along the top row, and your king guards a7 and b7.
questions.hintText: Your queen can reach the top row.

questions.question: White to move: Your two rooks work as a team. Find checkmate in 1 move!
questions.explanation: 1. Rb8# is checkmate! One rook guards the 7th row, and the other attacks the king on the 8th row.
questions.hintText: One rook already guards the 7th row. Use the other one.

questions.question: What is the opposite of 'early'?
questions.explanation: Early means before the usual time. Late means after it, so late is the opposite.
questions.hintText: Think of arriving at school after the bell has rung.

questions.question: Which word means the same as 'clever'?
questions.explanation: Clever and smart both describe someone who learns and understands things quickly.
questions.hintText: Think of a child who solves puzzles very quickly.

questions.question: What do we call a baby dog?
questions.explanation: A baby dog is a puppy. A kitten is a baby cat, a calf is a baby cow and a lamb is a baby sheep.
questions.hintText: It wags its little tail and loves to chew shoes.

questions.question: Which word is a verb (a doing word)?
questions.explanation: A verb tells what someone does. You can jump, so 'jump' is a verb.
questions.hintText: Pick the word for something you can do with your legs.

questions.question: What do we call a person who flies a plane?
questions.explanation: A pilot flies a plane. A driver drives a car, and a sailor works on a ship.
questions.hintText: This person sits at the very front, in the cockpit.

questions.question: Where can you borrow books to read at home?
questions.explanation: A library is a place full of books. You can borrow them and bring them back later.
questions.hintText: It is a quiet place with many shelves.

questions.question: What is the opposite of 'empty'?
questions.explanation: An empty glass has nothing in it. A full glass has no more room, so full is the opposite.
questions.hintText: Think of a glass with juice right up to the top.

questions.question: Which word means 'not afraid'?
questions.explanation: A brave person does something even when it feels a little scary.
questions.hintText: Think of a firefighter who helps people.

questions.question: Spring, summer, autumn and winter. What do we call these four?
questions.explanation: Spring, summer, autumn and winter are the four seasons of the year.
questions.hintText: They change the weather and come back every year.

questions.question: What do we call the meal we eat in the morning?
questions.explanation: Breakfast is the first meal of the day. Lunch comes at midday and dinner in the evening.
questions.hintText: It is the first meal after you wake up.

questions.question: Which word finishes the sentence? Birds fly with their ...
questions.explanation: Birds flap their wings to fly. Fish have fins, and cats have paws.
questions.hintText: Planes have them too, one on each side.

questions.question: What is a 'bug' in a computer program?
questions.optionsString: A picture on the screen|A mistake in the code|A very fast program|A secret password
questions.explanation: A bug is a mistake in the code. It makes the program do the wrong thing until someone fixes it.
questions.hintText: When a program has one, it does not work the way you wanted.

questions.question: A robot stands on square 1 and moves forward 3 squares. Which square is it on now?
questions.explanation: Start at 1 and count three steps: 2, 3, 4. The robot is on square 4.
questions.hintText: Count each step from the start square.

questions.question: A robot repeats 'jump, jump' 3 times. How many jumps does it make?
questions.explanation: Each round has 2 jumps. 3 rounds make 2 + 2 + 2 = 6 jumps.
questions.hintText: How many jumps are in one round?

questions.question: What do we call a list of step-by-step instructions for a computer?
questions.explanation: A program is a list of instructions. The computer follows them one step at a time.
questions.hintText: Games and apps are examples of it.

questions.question: A robot makes tea. Which step must come first?
questions.optionsString: Boil the water|Pour the tea|Drink the tea|Wash the cup
questions.explanation: Code runs in order. The robot must boil the water before it can pour and drink the tea.
questions.hintText: Which step do all the other steps need?

questions.question: IF the light is red, stop. ELSE go. The light is green. What does the robot do?
questions.optionsString: It stops|It goes|It turns back|It waits
questions.explanation: The light is not red, so the IF part is skipped. The robot follows ELSE and goes.
questions.hintText: ELSE means: in every other case.

questions.question: In code, what does a loop do?
questions.optionsString: Skips the steps|Deletes the steps|Repeats the steps|Hides the steps
questions.explanation: A loop repeats the same steps again and again, so you do not have to write them many times.
questions.hintText: Think of a song chorus that comes back again and again.

questions.question: A robot should take 2 steps, but its code says 'forward, forward, forward'. How do you fix it?
questions.explanation: The code has 3 'forward' steps, but the robot needs only 2. Remove one and the bug is fixed.
questions.hintText: Count the 'forward' steps in the code and compare.

questions.question: A box named 'score' holds the number 5. The code adds 1. What is in the box now?
questions.explanation: The box had 5. Adding 1 gives 5 + 1 = 6. In code, such a box is called a variable.
questions.hintText: The box keeps its number, and the code puts one more in.

questions.question: Line 1 says: show 'Hi'. Line 2 says: show 'Bye'. Which word shows first?
questions.explanation: A computer reads code from the top. Line 1 runs before line 2, so 'Hi' shows first.
questions.hintText: A computer starts at the top line and goes down.

questions.question: Which part of a computer do you use to type letters?
questions.explanation: You press the keys on the keyboard to type letters and numbers.
questions.hintText: It has many small buttons with letters on them.

packs.title: Tweens & Middle School (10–13 yrs): Smart STEM & Logic
packs.subtitle: Grades 5–8 percentages, speed & distance, solar eclipses, sequences & Python loops
packs.author: Kmito STEM Academy

questions.question: What is 25% (one quarter) of 100?
questions.hintText: A quarter means 4 equal parts. Split 100 into 4 groups.

questions.question: A train travels at a steady speed of 60 km/h for 2 hours. How many kilometers does it travel?
questions.explanation: Distance d = v × t = 60 km/h × 2 h = 120 km.
questions.hintText: The train covers 60 km every hour. How many such hours are there?

questions.question: What number comes next: 3, 6, 12, 24, ...?
questions.hintText: Find what you do to 3 to get 6, then to 6 to get 12.

questions.question: What causes a Solar Eclipse on Earth?
questions.optionsString: The Moon passes between the Sun and Earth|Earth passes into Mars's shadow|The Sun turns off briefly|Clouds block the sky
questions.explanation: A solar eclipse happens when the Moon moves directly between the Sun and Earth, casting a shadow on Earth.
questions.hintText: It is about a shadow falling on Earth. Which object must stand in front of the Sun?

questions.question: What does the adjective 'BENEVOLENT' mean?
questions.optionsString: Kind and well-meaning|Extremely loud|Hostile and angry|Freezing cold
questions.explanation: From Latin 'bene' (well/good), 'benevolent' means kind, generous, and well-meaning.
questions.hintText: Latin root 'bene' means good or well.

questions.question: In Python, how many times does the loop `for i in range(5):` repeat?
questions.explanation: range(5) generates the 5 integers 0, 1, 2, 3, 4 — so the loop runs exactly 5 times.
questions.hintText: Write out the numbers range(5) gives, starting at 0, and count them.

questions.question: What is 3/4 + 1/8 expressed in eighths?
questions.explanation: Convert to common denominator: 3/4 = 6/8. Then 6/8 + 1/8 = 7/8.
questions.hintText: Multiply the numerator and denominator of 3/4 by 2 to get eighths.

questions.question: Which layer of the Earth lies directly beneath the crust?
questions.explanation: The mantle is the thick silicate rock layer situated between Earth's crust and outer core.
questions.hintText: It makes up about 84% of Earth's total volume.

questions.question: What is the sum of the three interior angles of ANY triangle on a flat plane?
questions.explanation: On a flat Euclidean plane, the interior angles of any triangle always sum to 180°.
questions.hintText: Tear off the three corners of a paper triangle and line them up side by side.

questions.question: In Python, what is the index of the FIRST element in a list?
questions.explanation: In Python and most modern programming languages, array and list indexing starts at index 0.
questions.hintText: An index counts the items that come before it. How many come before the first?

questions.question: What is the scientific term when a solid turns directly into a gas without melting into liquid first?
questions.explanation: Sublimation is the phase transition directly from solid to gas (like dry ice solid CO₂).
questions.hintText: Think of dry ice turning directly into smoke-like gas at room temperature.

questions.question: A model car has a scale ratio of 1:10. If the real car is 250 cm long, how long is the model car?
questions.explanation: Scale 1:10 means divide by 10: 250 cm / 10 = 25 cm.
questions.hintText: 1:10 means every 10 cm of the real car becomes 1 cm on the model.

questions.question: Which cellular organelle is often called the 'powerhouse of the cell' for producing ATP energy?
questions.explanation: Mitochondria generate most of the chemical energy (ATP) needed to power cell reactions.
questions.hintText: Muscle cells need lots of energy, so they are packed with these.

questions.question: If 3x + 5 = 20, what is the value of 2x + 25?
questions.hintText: First solve for x by subtracting 5 from 20, then dividing by 3.

questions.question: An object has a mass of 60 grams and a volume of 20 cm³. What is its density?
questions.explanation: Density = Mass / Volume = 60 g / 20 cm³ = 3 g/cm³.
questions.hintText: Density = how many grams sit in each 1 cm³. Share the mass over the volume.

questions.question: In Python, what does 'Kmito'[0:4] evaluate to?
questions.explanation: Slice [0:4] takes characters at indices 0, 1, 2, and 3: 'K', 'm', 'i', 't'.
questions.hintText: A slice starts at index 0 and stops just before the end index.

questions.question: What is the area of a right-angled triangle with base 6 cm and height 8 cm?
questions.explanation: Area = (base × height) / 2 = (6 × 8) / 2 = 48 / 2 = 24 cm².
questions.hintText: A triangle is half of a rectangle with the same base and height.

questions.question: A simple lever has an effort arm of 4 meters and a load arm of 1 meter. What is its mechanical advantage?
questions.explanation: Mechanical advantage of a lever = Effort Arm / Load Arm = 4 m / 1 m = 4.
questions.hintText: Divide the effort arm length by the load arm length.

questions.question: What is the Least Common Multiple (LCM) of 4 and 6?
questions.explanation: Multiples of 4: 4, 8, 12... Multiples of 6: 6, 12... The smallest common multiple is 12.
questions.hintText: Find the smallest number that can be divided by both 4 and 6 without remainder.

questions.question: Which atmospheric gas is the most abundant by volume in Earth's air (~78%)?
questions.explanation: Nitrogen makes up approximately 78% of Earth's atmosphere, followed by oxygen at ~21%.
questions.hintText: This gas is a key ingredient of plant fertilizer.

questions.question: In Python, what is the result of the expression `(5 > 3) and (2 > 10)`?
questions.explanation: 5 > 3 is True, but 2 > 10 is False. In boolean AND, True and False produces False.
questions.hintText: Both conditions must be true for AND to evaluate to True.

questions.question: A cyclist travels 30 km in 40 minutes. What is their average speed in km/h?
questions.explanation: 40 minutes is 2/3 of an hour. Speed = 30 / (2/3) = 30 × 3 / 2 = 45 km/h.
questions.hintText: Convert 40 minutes to hours (2/3 hr), then speed = distance / time.

questions.question: Why does Earth experience four distinct seasons (Spring, Summer, Autumn, Winter)?
questions.optionsString: Earth's distance from the Sun changes dramatically|Earth's rotational axis is tilted by ~23.5 degrees|The Sun burns hotter during July and August|The Moon pulls Earth's climate bands
questions.explanation: Earth's 23.5° axial tilt causes different hemispheres to receive sunlight at different angles as it orbits the Sun.
questions.hintText: Why is it summer in the north while it is winter in the south at the same time?

questions.question: In a regular hexagon, what is the measure of each interior angle in degrees?
questions.hintText: The angles of a polygon add up to (n − 2) × 180°. All 6 here are equal.

questions.question: In Python, x starts at 1 and the loop `while x < 10: x *= 2` runs until it stops. What is x afterwards?
questions.explanation: x starts at 1, then becomes 2, 4, 8 (8 < 10 is true, so it doubles again) and 16. Now 16 < 10 is false, so the loop stops with x = 16.
questions.hintText: Keep doubling x. The loop stops when x is no longer below 10.

questions.question: A cube has surface area of 150 cm². What is the volume of this cube in cm³?
questions.explanation: A cube has 6 faces: 6a² = 150 => a² = 25 => a = 5 cm. Volume = a³ = 5³ = 125 cm³.
questions.hintText: Find the side length a first: 6 × a² = 150.

questions.question: When white light passes through a glass triangular prism, which color refracts (bends) the MOST?
questions.explanation: Violet light has the shortest wavelength in the visible spectrum and refracts the most through glass.
questions.hintText: Shorter wavelength bends more. Which end of the rainbow has the shortest?

questions.question: A jacket originally priced at $80 is discounted to $64. What is the percentage discount?
questions.hintText: How many dollars were taken off? Compare that with the ORIGINAL price.

questions.question: Three identical 6-Ohm resistors are connected in PARALLEL. What is the equivalent resistance?
questions.explanation: For parallel resistors: 1/R = 1/6 + 1/6 + 1/6 = 3/6 = 1/2 => R = 2 Ω.
questions.hintText: When n identical resistors are in parallel, equivalent R = R_single / n.

questions.question: Which data structure operates on a First-In, First-Out (FIFO) principle like a supermarket checkout line?
questions.explanation: A Queue processes elements FIFO (First In, First Out). A Stack is LIFO.
questions.hintText: Think of a pile of plates, where the last one added is used first. This one does the reverse.

questions.question: A fair coin is tossed 3 times. What is the total number of possible distinct outcome sequences?
questions.explanation: Each toss has 2 outcomes: 2 × 2 × 2 = 2³ = 8 outcomes (HHH, HHT, HTH, HTT, THH, THT, TTH, TTT).
questions.hintText: Each toss has 2 possible results. Multiply the choices for all the tosses.

questions.question: What is the name of the boundary around a black hole beyond which nothing, not even light, can escape?
questions.explanation: The Event Horizon is the theoretical boundary where the escape velocity exceeds the speed of light.
questions.hintText: The 'point of no return': cross it and you can never come back out.

questions.question: How many unique ways can 5 friends stand in a single line for a group photo (5!)?
questions.explanation: 5! = 5 × 4 × 3 × 2 × 1 = 120 unique permutations.
questions.hintText: 5 choices for the first spot, then one fewer for each next spot. Multiply them all.
questions.acceptedAnswers: one hundred twenty|one hundred and twenty

questions.question: At dawn the temperature is -3 °C. By noon it has risen by 8 degrees. What is the temperature at noon?
questions.explanation: Start at -3 and count up 8 steps: 3 steps take you to 0, and 5 more steps take you to 5 °C.
questions.hintText: Picture a thermometer: how many steps from -3 up to zero, and how many are left?

questions.question: What is 3/5 of 40?
questions.explanation: One fifth of 40 is 40 ÷ 5 = 8. Three fifths are 3 × 8 = 24.
questions.hintText: Find one fifth first, then take three of those parts.

questions.question: A rectangle is 9 cm long and 4 cm wide. What is its perimeter?
questions.explanation: The perimeter is the distance all the way around: 9 + 4 + 9 + 4 = 26 cm. (36 cm² would be the area.)
questions.hintText: Walk around the rectangle and add up all four sides.

questions.question: Which fraction is equal to the decimal 0.75?
questions.explanation: 0.75 means 75 hundredths: 75/100. Divide top and bottom by 25 to get 3/4.
questions.hintText: Write the decimal as hundredths, then simplify the fraction.

questions.question: What is 4 + 6 × 2? Remember the order of operations.
questions.explanation: Multiplication comes before addition: 6 × 2 = 12, then 4 + 12 = 16. Adding first would give 20, which is a common slip.
questions.hintText: Which comes first, adding or multiplying?

questions.question: What is the mean (average) of 4, 7 and 10?
questions.explanation: Add the numbers: 4 + 7 + 10 = 21. Then divide by how many there are: 21 ÷ 3 = 7.
questions.hintText: Add all the numbers, then share the total equally among them.

questions.question: A bag holds 3 red and 7 blue marbles. You take one without looking. What is the probability that it is red?
questions.explanation: There are 3 + 7 = 10 marbles in total and 3 of them are red, so the probability is 3/10. (3/7 compares red with blue, not with all.)
questions.hintText: Compare the red marbles with ALL the marbles in the bag.

questions.question: Mia and Ben share 30 stickers in the ratio 2:3. How many stickers does Ben get?
questions.explanation: The ratio 2:3 has 2 + 3 = 5 equal parts, so one part is 30 ÷ 5 = 6 stickers. Ben gets 3 parts: 3 × 6 = 18.
questions.hintText: How many equal parts does the ratio have in total? Find the size of one part first.

questions.question: There are 80 students in a grade, and 15% of them cycle to school. How many students cycle to school?
questions.explanation: 10% of 80 is 8, and 5% is half of that, 4. So 15% is 8 + 4 = 12 students.
questions.hintText: Find 10% first, then 5%, and put them together.

questions.question: Solve the equation 4x − 7 = 21. What is x?
questions.explanation: Add 7 to both sides: 4x = 28. Then divide by 4: x = 7.
questions.hintText: Undo the steps in reverse order: first the subtraction, then the multiplication.

questions.question: A box is 5 cm long, 4 cm wide and 3 cm high. What is its volume?
questions.explanation: Volume = length × width × height = 5 × 4 × 3 = 60 cm³. Adding the three numbers (12) is a common slip.
questions.hintText: Multiply the three edge lengths together.

questions.question: What is (-4) × (-6)?
questions.explanation: 4 × 6 = 24, and a negative times a negative gives a positive, so the answer is 24.
questions.hintText: Multiply the numbers first, then decide the sign: what do two minus signs make?

questions.question: What is 2/3 × 3/4 in its simplest form?
questions.explanation: Multiply tops and bottoms: (2 × 3)/(3 × 4) = 6/12. Divide both by 6 to simplify: 1/2.
questions.hintText: Multiply numerator by numerator and denominator by denominator, then simplify.

questions.question: What is the median of the numbers 5, 1, 9, 3 and 12?
questions.explanation: Put the numbers in order: 1, 3, 5, 9, 12. The median is the middle one, which is 5. (6 is the mean.)
questions.hintText: Sort the numbers from smallest to largest and look at the middle.

questions.question: After a 20% price rise, a board game costs 60 euros. What did it cost before the rise?
questions.explanation: The new price is 120% of the old one. So 1% is 60 ÷ 120 = 0.5 euros, and 100% is 50 euros. Taking 20% off 60 gives 48, which is the tempting wrong answer.
questions.hintText: The new price is 120% of the old price, not 100%.

questions.question: A right-angled triangle has two shorter sides of 9 cm and 12 cm. How long is its longest side (the hypotenuse)?
questions.explanation: Use a² + b² = c²: 9² + 12² = 81 + 144 = 225, and 225 = 15². So the hypotenuse is 15 cm.
questions.hintText: Use a² + b² = c², then take the square root.

questions.question: Solve 3(x + 4) = 2x + 20. What is the value of x?
questions.explanation: Open the bracket: 3x + 12 = 2x + 20. Take 2x from both sides: x + 12 = 20, so x = 8.
questions.hintText: Multiply out the bracket first: the 3 multiplies both terms inside.

questions.question: Two fair dice are rolled. What is the probability that both show a 6?
questions.explanation: Each die shows a 6 with probability 1/6. For both at once, multiply: 1/6 × 1/6 = 1/36.
questions.hintText: Find the chance for one die, then multiply the chances for the two dice.

questions.question: A circle has a radius of 5 cm. What is its area, written with π?
questions.explanation: Area = π × r² = π × 5² = 25π cm². (10π cm would be the circumference, 2πr.)
questions.hintText: Area uses the radius squared; circumference uses the radius doubled.

questions.question: In an isosceles triangle the angle at the top is 40°. How large is each of the two equal base angles?
questions.explanation: The three angles add up to 180°, so the two base angles share 180° − 40° = 140°. Each one is 140° ÷ 2 = 70°.
questions.hintText: All three angles make 180°. Take away the top angle, then split what is left.

questions.question: Three painters paint a fence in 6 hours. Working at the same pace, how long would two painters need?
questions.explanation: The whole job is 3 × 6 = 18 painter-hours of work. Two painters share it: 18 ÷ 2 = 9 hours. Fewer painters need more time, not less.
questions.hintText: How many hours would ONE painter need for the whole fence?

questions.question: Which expression is equal to 3(2a + 5) − 4a?
questions.explanation: Multiply out: 3 × 2a + 3 × 5 = 6a + 15. Then subtract 4a: 6a − 4a + 15 = 2a + 15.
questions.hintText: Multiply out the bracket, then collect the terms with a.

questions.question: Which force pulls a dropped ball towards the ground?
questions.explanation: Gravity is the pull between objects that have mass. Earth's gravity pulls the ball down towards its center.
questions.hintText: The same force keeps the Moon circling the Earth.

questions.question: At what temperature does pure water boil at sea level?
questions.explanation: At normal air pressure at sea level, pure water boils at 100 °C. The Celsius scale is built around this point and the freezing point, 0 °C.
questions.hintText: The Celsius scale puts freezing at 0 and boiling at a round number.

questions.question: Which gas do green plants take in from the air to make their food?
questions.explanation: In photosynthesis, plants use sunlight to turn carbon dioxide and water into sugar. They give off oxygen as they do it.
questions.hintText: It is the same gas that you breathe out.

questions.question: Which planet is closest to the Sun?
questions.explanation: Mercury is the innermost planet. Going outwards, the order starts Mercury, Venus, Earth, Mars.
questions.hintText: It is the smallest planet and races around the Sun in just 88 days.

questions.question: Which of these materials conducts electricity well?
questions.explanation: Copper is a metal, and metals let electric current flow easily. That is why wires are made of copper and covered in plastic, which does not conduct.
questions.hintText: Think about what is inside an electric cable.

questions.question: What is the energy of a moving object, such as a rolling ball, called?
questions.explanation: Kinetic energy is the energy an object has because it is moving. The faster and heavier the ball, the more kinetic energy it has.
questions.hintText: A parked car has none of it; a speeding car has a lot.

questions.question: In which unit is electric current measured?
questions.explanation: Electric current is measured in amperes (A). Volts measure voltage, ohms measure resistance and watts measure power.
questions.hintText: On a charger label it appears as a single capital letter after the number.

questions.question: Which part of a cell holds the DNA and controls what the cell does?
questions.explanation: The nucleus stores the cell's DNA, the instructions for building and running the cell. That is why it is called the control center.
questions.hintText: It is often drawn as a round blob near the middle of the cell.

questions.question: What is it called when a gas cools and turns into a liquid, like water droplets forming on a cold window?
questions.explanation: Condensation is the change from gas to liquid. Water vapor in the air cools on the cold glass and becomes tiny drops.
questions.hintText: The same change makes clouds form high in the sky.

questions.question: What is the main source of energy that drives Earth's water cycle?
questions.explanation: The Sun's heat evaporates water from seas, lakes and land. The vapor rises, cools into clouds and falls again as rain or snow.
questions.hintText: What makes a puddle dry up faster on a bright day?

questions.question: A box is pushed to the right with a force of 12 N. Friction pushes back with 5 N. What is the net force on the box?
questions.optionsString: 17 N to the right|7 N to the left|7 N to the right|60 N to the right
questions.explanation: The two forces act in opposite directions, so subtract them: 12 N − 5 N = 7 N. The push is bigger, so the net force points to the right.
questions.hintText: Forces in opposite directions work against each other. Which one is bigger?

questions.question: A 12-volt battery sends a current of 3 amperes through a lamp. What is the lamp's resistance?
questions.explanation: Ohm's law says resistance = voltage ÷ current: 12 V ÷ 3 A = 4 Ω. Multiplying instead (36) is the usual slip.
questions.hintText: Ohm's law: resistance is voltage divided by current.

questions.question: Light travels at about 300 000 km per second. Roughly how long does sunlight take to reach Earth?
questions.explanation: The Sun is about 150 million km away. 150 000 000 ÷ 300 000 = 500 seconds, which is a little over 8 minutes.
questions.hintText: The Sun is about 150 million km away. Divide the distance by the speed.

questions.question: A liquid has a pH of 3. What kind of liquid is it?
questions.explanation: The pH scale runs from 0 to 14. Below 7 is acidic, exactly 7 is neutral and above 7 is basic. So pH 3 is acidic, like lemon juice.
questions.hintText: Pure water sits in the middle of the scale at pH 7. Which side is this liquid on?

questions.question: Why do we always see the same side of the Moon from Earth?
questions.optionsString: The Moon does not turn on its axis at all|The Moon turns once per trip around Earth|Earth's shadow always hides the other side|The other side never reflects any sunlight
questions.explanation: The Moon turns once on its axis in the same time it takes to go once around Earth, about 27 days. So the same face always points towards us.
questions.hintText: Walk around a chair while always facing it. Did your body turn?

questions.question: What number comes next: 1, 4, 9, 16, ...?
questions.explanation: These are the square numbers: 1 × 1, 2 × 2, 3 × 3, 4 × 4. The next is 5 × 5 = 25. (The gaps 3, 5, 7 grow by 2 each time, so the next gap is 9.)
questions.hintText: Look at the gaps between the numbers. How do the gaps grow?

questions.question: Tom is taller than Ana. Ana is taller than Leo. Who is the shortest?
questions.explanation: Put them in order from tallest to shortest: Tom, Ana, Leo. So Leo is the shortest.
questions.hintText: Line the three children up from tallest to shortest.

questions.question: In a race you overtake the runner in second place. What place are you in now?
questions.explanation: You take the place of the runner you passed, so you are now second. The runner in first place is still ahead of you.
questions.hintText: Whose place do you take when you pass someone?

questions.question: What number comes next: 1, 1, 2, 3, 5, 8, ...?
questions.explanation: Each number is the sum of the two before it: 3 + 5 = 8, so next comes 5 + 8 = 13. This is the famous Fibonacci sequence.
questions.hintText: Add two neighbors together and compare with the number after them.

questions.question: Sara is twice as old as her brother. Together they are 18 years old. How old is Sara?
questions.explanation: Think of the brother's age as 1 part and Sara's as 2 parts: 3 parts make 18, so 1 part is 6. Sara is 2 × 6 = 12, and her brother is 6.
questions.hintText: Count the brother as one part and Sara as two parts. How many parts make the total?

questions.question: If the day after tomorrow is Friday, what day was yesterday?
questions.explanation: The day after tomorrow is Friday, so tomorrow is Thursday and today is Wednesday. Yesterday was therefore Tuesday.
questions.hintText: Work out what day it is today first.

questions.question: A drawer holds 10 red socks and 10 blue socks. In the dark, how many socks must you take out to be sure of getting two of the same color?
questions.explanation: With two socks you might get one red and one blue. The third sock must match one of them, because there are only two colors. So 3 socks are enough.
questions.hintText: Imagine the unluckiest start: your first socks all have different colors.

questions.question: A snail climbs a 10 m wall. Each day it climbs 3 m, and each night it slides back 2 m. On which day does it first reach the top?
questions.explanation: The snail gains 1 m per full day and night, so after 7 nights it is at 7 m. On day 8 it climbs 3 m and reaches 10 m before it can slide back.
questions.hintText: Once the snail reaches the top during the day, it no longer slides back.

questions.question: One of three boxes holds a prize. Box A says: 'The prize is here.' Box B says: 'The prize is not here.' Box C says: 'The prize is not in box A.' Only one label is true. Where is the prize?
questions.optionsString: Box A|Box B|Box C|It cannot be known
questions.explanation: Test each box. In A, labels A and B would both be true; in C, labels B and C would both be true. In B, only label C is true, so the prize is in box B.
questions.hintText: Try each box in turn and count how many labels would be true.

questions.question: Whenever it rains, the street gets wet. This morning the street is wet. What do we know for certain?
questions.optionsString: It definitely rained|It definitely did not rain|Maybe it rained, maybe not|The first sentence is false
questions.explanation: We only know what rain does. A wet street could also come from a street-cleaning truck or a burst pipe, so rain is possible but not certain.
questions.hintText: Can you think of another way a street could get wet?

questions.question: You have 9 coins that look the same, but one is slightly heavier. Using a balance scale, what is the smallest number of weighings that always finds it?
questions.explanation: Weigh 3 coins against 3: the heavier group, or the 3 left out if they balance, holds the heavy coin. Then weigh 1 of those 3 against another: the heavier one, or the one left out, is it. That makes 2 weighings.
questions.hintText: Split the coins into three equal groups instead of two.

questions.question: A patch of water lilies doubles in size every day. On day 30 it covers the whole pond. On which day did it cover half the pond?
questions.explanation: The patch doubles each day, so one day before the pond was full it was half full. That is day 29, not day 15.
questions.hintText: Work backwards from the last day: what was the size one day earlier?

questions.question: A program sets x = 3 and then runs x = x + 4. What is the value of x now?
questions.explanation: The computer first works out the right-hand side with the old value: 3 + 4 = 7. Then it stores that result back in x.
questions.hintText: Work out the right-hand side with the old value of x, then store the result.

questions.question: What is a 'bug' in a computer program?
questions.optionsString: A mistake in the code|A very fast loop|A kind of password|A copy of a saved file
questions.explanation: A bug is a mistake in a program that makes it behave in the wrong way. Finding and fixing bugs is called debugging.
questions.hintText: Programmers hunt for these and remove them so the program works properly.
questions.acceptedAnswers: a mistake|an error|error in the code|mistake

questions.question: A program has x = 8. It says: if x is greater than 5, print 'big', otherwise print 'small'. What does it print?
questions.explanation: The condition asks whether 8 is greater than 5. That is true, so the program takes the first branch and prints 'big'.
questions.hintText: Check the condition with the real value of x: is it true or false?

questions.question: What is the binary number 101 written as an ordinary decimal number?
questions.explanation: From right to left the binary places are worth 1, 2 and 4. The number 101 has the 4 and the 1 switched on: 4 + 0 + 1 = 5.
questions.hintText: The binary places are worth 1, 2, 4, 8, ... from right to left. Add the ones that are on.

questions.question: A program starts with total = 0. Then, for each number n in 1, 2, 3, 4, it runs total = total + n. What is total at the end?
questions.explanation: The loop adds each number in turn: 0 + 1 = 1, then 3, then 6, then 10. So total ends at 10.
questions.hintText: Follow the loop step by step and write down total after each round.

questions.question: In Python, the % operator gives the remainder of a division. What is 17 % 5?
questions.explanation: 5 fits into 17 three times, which makes 15. The remainder is 17 − 15 = 2. (3 is the whole-number quotient, not the remainder.)
questions.hintText: How many whole times does 5 fit into 17, and what is left over?

questions.question: A loop that repeats 3 times contains a second loop that repeats 4 times. The inner loop prints one star each time it runs. How many stars are printed in total?
questions.explanation: Every time the outer loop runs once, the inner loop runs 4 times. With 3 outer rounds that is 3 × 4 = 12 stars. Adding (3 + 4 = 7) is the tempting slip.
questions.hintText: How many stars appear during ONE round of the outer loop?

questions.question: A bit can be 0 or 1. How many different patterns can be made with 4 bits?
questions.explanation: Each extra bit doubles the number of patterns: 2 × 2 × 2 × 2 = 16. They run from 0000 to 1111.
questions.hintText: One bit gives 2 patterns, two bits give 4. What happens each time you add a bit?

questions.question: A function is defined as f(n) = n × n + 1. What is f(f(2))?
questions.explanation: Work from the inside out: f(2) = 2 × 2 + 1 = 5. Then f(5) = 5 × 5 + 1 = 26.
questions.hintText: Start with the inner call, then feed its result into the function again.

questions.question: What does the prefix 'kilo-' mean, as in kilometer and kilogram?
questions.explanation: 'Kilo-' means one thousand. A kilometer is 1000 meters and a kilogram is 1000 grams.
questions.hintText: How many meters are in one kilometer?

questions.question: What does the word part 'micro-' mean, as in microscope and microphone?
questions.explanation: 'Micro-' comes from Greek and means very small. A microscope lets you see things that are too small for the eye alone.
questions.hintText: Think about what kind of things you look at through a microscope.

questions.question: In space science, what is an 'orbit'?
questions.optionsString: The glowing tail behind a comet|A large group of distant stars|The shadow cast by a planet|The path of one object around another
questions.explanation: An orbit is the curved path one object follows around another, held by gravity. Earth's orbit around the Sun takes one year.
questions.hintText: Earth completes one of these around the Sun every year.

questions.question: What does the word ending '-logy' mean, as in biology and geology?
questions.optionsString: The study of|The fear of|The love of|The lack of
questions.explanation: '-logy' comes from Greek and means 'the study of'. Biology is the study of living things and geology is the study of the Earth.
questions.hintText: Think about what biologists and geologists do with their subjects.

questions.question: What does the word part 'photo-' mean, as in photosynthesis and photograph?
questions.explanation: 'Photo-' comes from the Greek word for light. Photosynthesis means 'putting together with light', and a photograph is 'drawn with light'.
questions.hintText: Plants need it for photosynthesis, and a camera needs it too.

questions.question: What does the word part 'hydro-' mean, as in hydroelectric and hydrant?
questions.explanation: 'Hydro-' comes from the Greek word for water. A hydroelectric plant makes electricity from flowing water, and a hydrant supplies water to firefighters.
questions.hintText: Think about what comes out of a fire hydrant.

questions.question: What does the word part 'chrono-' mean, as in chronological and chronometer?
questions.explanation: 'Chrono-' comes from the Greek word for time. Chronological order puts events in the order they happened in time, and a chronometer is a very exact clock.
questions.hintText: A chronometer is an instrument. Think about what it measures.

questions.question: What does the Latin root 'equ-' mean, as in equator and equivalent?
questions.explanation: 'Equ-' comes from the Latin word for 'same' or 'level'. The equator divides the Earth into two halves of the same size, and equivalent things have the same value.
questions.hintText: The equator splits the Earth into two halves. How do the halves compare?

questions.question: In science, what is a 'hypothesis'?
questions.optionsString: A result that has been proven true|A table of measured values|A tool for exact measuring|An idea that can be tested
questions.explanation: A hypothesis is a reasoned guess that scientists can test with an experiment. The results then support it or show that it is wrong.
questions.hintText: It comes at the start of an investigation, before the experiment is done.
questions.acceptedAnswers: a testable idea|an educated guess|a guess that can be tested

packs.title: Teens & High School (14–17 yrs): Exam & IQ Booster
packs.subtitle: Pythagorean geometry, syllogisms, Newton's laws, binary math & logarithms
packs.author: Kmito Olympiad Prep

questions.question: If a right triangle has legs a = 5 and b = 12, what is the hypotenuse c?
questions.explanation: By the Pythagorean Theorem: c = √(5² + 12²) = √(25 + 144) = √169 = 13.
questions.hintText: Use a² + b² = c², then take a square root.

questions.question: All metals conduct electricity. Copper is a metal. What follows logically?
questions.optionsString: Copper conducts electricity|All conductors are copper|Copper is an insulator|Some metals do not conduct
questions.explanation: By universal instantiation (Modus Ponens): if every member of set M has property E, and C ∈ M, then C has property E.
questions.hintText: Apply the rule for all metals to copper.

questions.question: What net force F (in Newtons) is required to accelerate a 5 kg mass at 4 m/s²?
questions.explanation: By Newton's Second Law: F = m × a = 5 kg × 4 m/s² = 20 N.
questions.hintText: Use Newton's second law: force = mass × acceleration.

questions.question: Choose the best synonym for 'PRAGMATIC':
questions.explanation: 'Pragmatic' means dealing with things sensibly and realistically in a practical way.
questions.hintText: Picture someone who picks whatever actually works, whatever the theory says.

questions.question: What is the decimal (base-10) value of the 4-bit binary number 1010₂?
questions.hintText: Read the bits from the right as 1, 2, 4, 8 and add the places that hold a 1.

questions.question: What is log₂(256)? (To what power must 2 be raised to equal 256?)
questions.explanation: Since 2⁸ = 256, log₂(256) = 8.
questions.hintText: Keep doubling 2 and count how many 2s you multiply to reach 256.

questions.question: For any angle θ, what is the exact value of sin²(θ) + cos²(θ)?
questions.explanation: The fundamental Pythagorean trigonometric identity states sin²(θ) + cos²(θ) = 1.
questions.hintText: Picture the point (cos θ, sin θ) on the unit circle and apply Pythagoras.

questions.question: What is the pH value of pure neutral water at 25 °C?
questions.explanation: Pure water has equal concentrations of H⁺ and OH⁻ ions, yielding a neutral pH of exactly 7.
questions.hintText: Acids have a low pH and bases a high pH; neutral sits exactly between them.

questions.question: What is the value of log₁₀(1000)?
questions.hintText: Count the zeros: 10 to what power gives 1000?

questions.question: How many bits are in one standard Byte?
questions.explanation: 1 Byte is defined as exactly 8 bits (capable of representing 256 distinct values).
questions.hintText: One byte can store any number from 0 to 255. How many binary digits does that take?

questions.question: For ax² + bx + c = 0, what does a discriminant D = b² - 4ac > 0 indicate about the roots?
questions.optionsString: No real roots (two complex roots)|Two distinct real roots|Exactly one real root (multiplicity 2)|All roots are zero
questions.explanation: When D > 0, the quadratic formula yields two distinct real solutions.
questions.hintText: Put a positive D into x = (−b ± √D) / 2a and count the different results.

questions.question: What is the kinetic energy (in Joules) of an 8 kg projectile moving at 10 m/s (E = ½mv²)?
questions.hintText: Square only the speed, and don't forget the ½.

questions.question: What is the magnitude (length) of 2D vector v = (3, 4)?
questions.hintText: Use the Pythagorean theorem: √(x² + y²).

questions.question: A sound wave has a frequency of 170 Hz and travels at 340 m/s in air. What is its wavelength λ?
questions.explanation: λ = v / f = 340 m/s / 170 Hz = 2.0 meters.
questions.hintText: Wavelength is the wave speed divided by the frequency.

questions.question: What is the decimal value of the hexadecimal number 0x1F?
questions.hintText: The left digit counts in sixteens, and the hex digit F is worth 15.

questions.question: If log₂(x) + log₂(4) = 3, what is x?
questions.hintText: log(a) + log(b) = log(ab), so log₂(4x) = 3.

questions.question: Which device transforms electrical energy into mechanical rotational kinetic energy?
questions.explanation: An electric motor converts electrical energy into rotational mechanical motion using Lorentz forces.
questions.hintText: Think of what spins a washing-machine drum or the wheels of an electric car.

questions.question: How many combinations of 3 books can be chosen from a shelf of 5 books (C(5, 3))?
questions.hintText: Picking 3 books to take is the same as picking the 2 books to leave behind.

questions.question: According to De Morgan's Law, what is NOT (A AND B) equivalent to?
questions.optionsString: (NOT A) AND (NOT B)|(NOT A) OR (NOT B)|NOT (A OR B)|A OR B
questions.explanation: De Morgan's first law: ¬(A ∧ B) ≡ (¬A) ∨ (¬B).
questions.hintText: Check with a truth table: try A = true, B = false in each option.

questions.question: What is absolute zero in degrees Celsius (the temperature at which thermal motion ceases)?
questions.explanation: Absolute zero (0 Kelvin) corresponds to -273.15 °C.
questions.hintText: Kelvin and Celsius degrees are the same size; only the starting point differs.

questions.question: What is the infinite sum S = 2 + 1 + 1/2 + 1/4 + 1/8 + ...?
questions.explanation: Formula S = a / (1 - r) with initial term a = 2 and common ratio r = 1/2: S = 2 / (1 - 0.5) = 4.
questions.hintText: Geometric series: sum = first term ÷ (1 − common ratio). Find the ratio first.

questions.question: If a radioactive isotope has a half-life of 4 hours, what fraction remains after 12 hours?
questions.explanation: 12 hours = 3 half-lives. Remaining fraction = (1/2)³ = 1/8.
questions.hintText: Count how many 4-hour half-lives fit in 12 hours, then halve once for each.

questions.question: What is the area of a trapezoid with parallel bases 8 cm and 12 cm, and height 6 cm?
questions.hintText: Area = average of the two parallel bases × height.

questions.question: What is the average time complexity of searching in a Balanced Binary Search Tree (AVL or Red-Black)?
questions.explanation: Because the height of a balanced tree with n nodes is bounded by log₂(n), search takes O(log n).
questions.hintText: Each step cuts the remaining search space in half.

questions.question: What optical phenomenon explains why diamonds exhibit such brilliant sparkle?
questions.explanation: Diamonds have a high refractive index (2.42) and small critical angle (~24.4°), trapping light via total internal reflection.
questions.hintText: What does light do at the inner wall of a glass block when it hits at a big angle?

questions.question: What is the instantaneous rate of change (derivative dy/dx) of y = x² at the point where x = 1?
questions.explanation: The power rule gives dy/dx = 2x. Evaluated at x = 1, the slope is 2(1) = 2.
questions.hintText: Use the power rule d/dx xⁿ = n·xⁿ⁻¹, then plug in x = 1.

questions.question: According to Einstein's mass-energy equivalence equation E = mc², what does 'c' represent?
questions.optionsString: Speed of light in vacuum|Speed of sound|Capacitance|Coulomb's constant
questions.explanation: In E = mc², c is the speed of light in vacuum (~3 × 10⁸ m/s).
questions.hintText: Check the units: a joule is kg·m²/s², so what kind of quantity is c?
questions.acceptedAnswers: speed of light|the speed of light|light speed|velocity of light

questions.question: How many total possible outcomes exist when rolling three standard 6-sided dice simultaneously (6³)?
questions.explanation: Each die has 6 faces: 6 × 6 × 6 = 6³ = 216 distinct outcomes.
questions.hintText: Each die has 6 outcomes whatever the others show, so multiply them.

questions.question: What is the result of the bitwise XOR operation `5 ^ 3` (in binary: `101₂ ^ 011₂`)?
questions.hintText: XOR gives 1 only where the two bits differ; go column by column.

questions.question: According to Bernoulli's principle, when the velocity of a flowing fluid increases, what happens to its static pressure?
questions.optionsString: It decreases|It increases|It remains constant|It becomes negative
questions.explanation: Bernoulli's principle states that an increase in fluid speed occurs simultaneously with a decrease in static pressure.
questions.hintText: Think how a plane wing gets lift: air moves faster over its curved top.

questions.question: What is the probability of rolling a sum of 8 with two fair 6-sided dice?
questions.explanation: Pairs summing to 8: (2,6), (3,5), (4,4), (5,3), (6,2) — exactly 5 combinations out of 36.
questions.hintText: Count ordered pairs, so (2, 6) and (6, 2) are different outcomes.

questions.question: What does the Heisenberg Uncertainty Principle state cannot be measured simultaneously with arbitrary precision?
questions.optionsString: Mass and charge|Position and momentum|Temperature and pressure|Velocity and acceleration
questions.explanation: Heisenberg's principle states Δx × Δp ≥ ℏ/2; exact position and momentum cannot both be known simultaneously.
questions.hintText: Δx · Δp ≥ ℏ/2 — think about what the letters x and p stand for.

questions.question: What is 17 mod 5?
questions.explanation: 17 = 3 × 5 + 2, so the remainder (17 mod 5) is 2.
questions.hintText: mod means remainder after division: how many whole 5s fit in 17?

questions.question: What value of x solves 5x − 8 = 2x + 13?
questions.explanation: Subtract 2x and add 8 on both sides: 3x = 21, so x = 7.
questions.hintText: Collect the x terms on one side and the plain numbers on the other.

questions.question: What is the slope of the straight line through the points (1, 2) and (4, 11)?
questions.explanation: Slope = change in y ÷ change in x = (11 − 2) ÷ (4 − 1) = 9 ÷ 3 = 3.
questions.hintText: Divide the change in y by the change in x.

questions.question: If f(x) = 2x² − 3x + 1, what is f(3)?
questions.explanation: f(3) = 2 × 3² − 3 × 3 + 1 = 18 − 9 + 1 = 10. Square the 3 first, then multiply by 2.
questions.hintText: Replace every x with 3 and square before you multiply.

questions.question: What is the exact value of sin 30°?
questions.explanation: In a 30°–60°–90° triangle the side opposite 30° is half the hypotenuse, so sin 30° = 1/2. √3/2 is sin 60°.
questions.hintText: Think of half an equilateral triangle: compare the short side with the hypotenuse.

questions.question: An arithmetic sequence starts 7, 11, 15, 19, ... What is its 10th term?
questions.explanation: The common difference is 4. The 10th term is 7 + 9 × 4 = 43: there are only 9 steps from the 1st to the 10th term.
questions.hintText: Use aₙ = a₁ + (n − 1)·d and count the steps, not the terms.

questions.question: A bag holds 4 red and 6 blue marbles. One marble is drawn at random. What is the probability that it is red?
questions.explanation: There are 4 red marbles among 10 in total, so P(red) = 4/10 = 2/5. 2/3 compares red with blue instead of with all marbles.
questions.hintText: Divide the favourable outcomes by the total number of marbles.

questions.question: Which expression is equal to x³ · x⁴?
questions.explanation: When powers with the same base are multiplied, the exponents are added: x³ · x⁴ = x³⁺⁴ = x⁷. Multiplying the exponents would give (x³)⁴ = x¹².
questions.hintText: Write out x·x·x times x·x·x·x and count the factors.

questions.question: The price of a jacket rises from 80 € to 100 €. By what percentage did the price increase?
questions.explanation: The increase is 20 €, measured against the old price: 20 ÷ 80 = 0.25 = 25%. Dividing by the new price (20 ÷ 100) gives the tempting 20%.
questions.hintText: Compare the increase with the original price, not with the new one.

questions.question: What are the solutions of the equation x² − 5x + 6 = 0?
questions.optionsString: x = -2 and x = -3|x = 2 and x = 3|x = 1 and x = 6|x = -1 and x = 6
questions.explanation: Factor: x² − 5x + 6 = (x − 2)(x − 3), so x = 2 or x = 3. Check: the roots add up to 5 and multiply to 6.
questions.hintText: Find two numbers whose product is 6 and whose sum is 5.

questions.question: What are the coordinates of the vertex of the parabola y = x² − 6x + 5?
questions.explanation: The vertex lies at x = −b ÷ (2a) = 6 ÷ 2 = 3. Then y = 3² − 6 × 3 + 5 = 9 − 18 + 5 = −4, so the vertex is (3, −4).
questions.hintText: The vertex is at x = −b ÷ (2a); put that x back into the equation.

questions.question: In a right triangle, sin θ = 3/5 for an acute angle θ. What is cos θ?
questions.explanation: Use sin²θ + cos²θ = 1: cos²θ = 1 − 9/25 = 16/25, so cos θ = 4/5 (positive, because θ is acute). It is the 3-4-5 triangle.
questions.hintText: Use sin²θ + cos²θ = 1, or sketch the triangle and find the missing side.

questions.question: Given that log₁₀(2) ≈ 0.301, what is log₁₀(200) to three decimal places?
questions.hintText: Split 200 into a product and use log(ab) = log(a) + log(b).

questions.question: How many different 3-digit numbers can be formed from the digits 1, 2, 3, 4 and 5 if no digit is repeated?
questions.explanation: There are 5 choices for the first digit, 4 for the second and 3 for the third: 5 × 4 × 3 = 60. Order matters here, so it is not C(5, 3) = 10.
questions.hintText: Count the choices left for each position in turn and multiply them.

questions.question: A geometric sequence starts 3, 6, 12, 24, ... What is its 8th term?
questions.explanation: The common ratio is 2, so the 8th term is 3 × 2⁷ = 3 × 128 = 384. The exponent is 7 because there are 7 steps from the 1st to the 8th term.
questions.hintText: Use aₙ = a₁ · rⁿ⁻¹: the exponent is one less than the term number.

questions.question: A fair coin is tossed 4 times. What is the probability of getting exactly 2 heads?
questions.explanation: There are 2⁴ = 16 equally likely sequences, and C(4, 2) = 6 of them contain exactly 2 heads. So P = 6/16 = 3/8, not 1/2.
questions.hintText: Count all possible sequences, then the ways to place the 2 heads among the 4 tosses.

questions.question: How many positive divisors does the number 360 have?
questions.explanation: 360 = 2³ × 3² × 5. A divisor picks 0–3 twos, 0–2 threes and 0–1 fives, so there are 4 × 3 × 2 = 24 divisors.
questions.hintText: Find the prime factorisation, add 1 to each exponent and multiply the results.

questions.question: The roots of x² − 6x + 4 = 0 are p and q. What is the value of p² + q²?
questions.explanation: By Vieta's formulas p + q = 6 and pq = 4. Then p² + q² = (p + q)² − 2pq = 36 − 8 = 28.
questions.hintText: You do not need the roots: use p + q and pq with (p + q)² = p² + 2pq + q².

questions.question: In a triangle, two sides are 5 cm and 8 cm long and the angle between them is 60°. How long is the third side?
questions.explanation: Law of cosines: c² = 5² + 8² − 2 × 5 × 8 × cos 60° = 25 + 64 − 40 = 49, so c = 7 cm. √89 would be right only for a 90° angle.
questions.hintText: Use the law of cosines: c² = a² + b² − 2ab·cos γ, with cos 60° = 1/2.

questions.question: Which values of x solve log₂(x − 1) + log₂(x + 1) = 3?
questions.optionsString: Only x = 3|Only x = -3|x = 3 and x = -3|Only x = 4
questions.explanation: Combine the logs: log₂((x − 1)(x + 1)) = 3, so x² − 1 = 8 and x = ±3. Only x = 3 works, because for x = −3 the logarithm of a negative number is not defined.
questions.hintText: Combine the logarithms into one, then check each candidate in the original equation.

questions.question: How many zeros are at the end of the number 25! (25 factorial)?
questions.explanation: Each trailing zero needs a factor 2 × 5, and fives are the scarce ones. The multiples of 5 up to 25 give 5 fives, and 25 = 5 × 5 gives one more: 6 zeros.
questions.hintText: Count how many factors of 5 appear in 1 × 2 × ... × 25; watch out for 25 itself.

questions.question: Let f(x) = 2x + 3 and g(x) = x². What is g(f(2)) − f(g(2))?
questions.explanation: f(2) = 7, so g(f(2)) = 7² = 49. g(2) = 4, so f(g(2)) = 2 × 4 + 3 = 11. The difference is 49 − 11 = 38: the order of composition matters.
questions.hintText: Work from the inside out: evaluate the inner function first, then the outer one.

questions.question: How many integers n satisfy n² < 50?
questions.explanation: n² < 50 holds for n from −7 to 7, because 7² = 49 and 8² = 64. That is 7 negative integers, 7 positive integers and 0: 15 in total.
questions.hintText: Integers include negative numbers and zero, not only positive numbers.

questions.question: A 4 Ω resistor is connected to a 12 V battery. What current flows through it?
questions.explanation: Ohm's law: I = U ÷ R = 12 V ÷ 4 Ω = 3 A. Multiplying instead of dividing gives the wrong value 48.
questions.hintText: Use Ohm's law: current = voltage ÷ resistance.

questions.question: A cyclist speeds up steadily from rest to 12 m/s in 6 s. What is the acceleration?
questions.explanation: Acceleration = change in speed ÷ time = 12 m/s ÷ 6 s = 2 m/s².
questions.hintText: Divide the change in speed by the time it takes.

questions.question: Which cell organelle releases most of the cell's usable energy (ATP) through aerobic respiration?
questions.explanation: Mitochondria carry out aerobic respiration and make most of the cell's ATP. Ribosomes build proteins, and the nucleus stores the DNA.
questions.hintText: It is often called the powerhouse of the cell.

questions.question: A sodium atom has atomic number 11 and mass number 23. How many neutrons are in its nucleus?
questions.explanation: The mass number counts protons plus neutrons, and the atomic number counts protons. So neutrons = 23 − 11 = 12.
questions.hintText: The mass number is protons plus neutrons; the atomic number is protons only.

questions.question: Which of these electromagnetic waves has the shortest wavelength?
questions.explanation: In order of decreasing wavelength: radio waves, microwaves, infrared, visible light, ultraviolet, X-rays, gamma rays. Of the four listed, X-rays are the shortest.
questions.hintText: Shorter wavelength means higher frequency and more energy per photon.

questions.question: A stone is dropped from rest and falls freely for 3 s. How far does it fall? (Take g = 10 m/s² and ignore air resistance.)
questions.explanation: s = ½ × g × t² = ½ × 10 × 3² = 5 × 9 = 45 m. 30 m would be right only if the stone fell at a steady 10 m/s.
questions.hintText: Use s = ½·g·t² and square the time before multiplying.

questions.question: Resistors of 6 Ω and 3 Ω are connected in parallel. What is their combined resistance?
questions.explanation: For parallel resistors 1/R = 1/6 + 1/3 = 1/2, so R = 2 Ω. The result is always smaller than the smallest single resistor; 9 Ω is the series value.
questions.hintText: In parallel the reciprocals add: 1/R = 1/R₁ + 1/R₂.

questions.question: An electric kettle draws a current of 10 A from a 230 V supply. What is its power?
questions.explanation: Electric power P = U × I = 230 V × 10 A = 2300 W, which is 2.3 kW.
questions.hintText: Electric power is voltage multiplied by current.

questions.question: How many moles of water are in 36 g of water? (Molar mass of H₂O: 18 g/mol.)
questions.explanation: Amount of substance n = m ÷ M = 36 g ÷ 18 g/mol = 2 mol. Dividing the other way round gives 0.5.
questions.hintText: Divide the mass by the molar mass.

questions.question: In a DNA molecule, which base pairs with adenine?
questions.explanation: In DNA adenine pairs with thymine and guanine pairs with cytosine. Uracil replaces thymine only in RNA.
questions.hintText: A always faces the same partner; the DNA alphabet has only four letters: A, C, G, T.

questions.question: A car travelling at 20 m/s brakes with a constant deceleration of 5 m/s². How far does it travel before it stops?
questions.explanation: From v² = 2 × a × s: s = v² ÷ (2a) = 400 ÷ 10 = 40 m. Check: it stops after 4 s at an average speed of 10 m/s, which is also 40 m.
questions.hintText: Use v² = 2·a·s, or find the braking time and the average speed.

questions.question: A 2 kg trolley moving at 6 m/s hits a stationary 4 kg trolley and they stick together. How fast do they move just after the collision?
questions.explanation: Momentum is conserved: 2 kg × 6 m/s = 12 kg·m/s before, and (2 + 4) kg × v after. So v = 12 ÷ 6 = 2 m/s.
questions.hintText: Total momentum (mass × velocity) is the same before and after the collision.

questions.question: A 12 V battery is connected to a 2 Ω and a 4 Ω resistor in series. What is the voltage across the 4 Ω resistor?
questions.explanation: The total resistance is 2 + 4 = 6 Ω, so the current is 12 V ÷ 6 Ω = 2 A. Across the 4 Ω resistor: U = I × R = 2 A × 4 Ω = 8 V.
questions.hintText: Find the current through the whole circuit first, then apply U = I·R to one resistor.

questions.question: What is the pH of a 0.001 mol/L solution of hydrochloric acid (HCl, a strong acid)?
questions.explanation: A strong acid is fully dissociated, so [H⁺] = 0.001 = 10⁻³ mol/L. pH = −log₁₀[H⁺] = 3. The value 11 is the pOH of this solution.
questions.hintText: pH = −log₁₀ of the H⁺ concentration; write the concentration as a power of 10.

questions.question: The length of a simple pendulum is made 4 times longer. How does its period of swing change?
questions.optionsString: It becomes 4 times longer|It becomes 16 times longer|It stays the same|It becomes 2 times longer
questions.explanation: The period is T = 2π√(l ÷ g), so it grows with the square root of the length. √4 = 2, so the period becomes 2 times longer.
questions.hintText: The period depends on the square root of the length: T = 2π√(l ÷ g).
questions.acceptedAnswers: It doubles|doubles|2 times longer|twice as long

questions.question: Which number comes next in the pattern 2, 6, 12, 20, 30, ...?
questions.explanation: The differences grow by 2 each time: +4, +6, +8, +10, so the next step is +12 and 30 + 12 = 42. Each term is also n × (n + 1).
questions.hintText: Write down the differences between neighbouring numbers and see how they change.

questions.question: If it is raining, the street is wet. The street is not wet. What follows logically?
questions.optionsString: It is raining|It rained earlier|It is not raining|Nothing follows
questions.explanation: If rain always makes the street wet, a dry street rules out rain. This rule is called modus tollens: from 'if P then Q' and 'not Q' follows 'not P'.
questions.hintText: Ask yourself: could the street be dry if rain were falling right now?

questions.question: Anna is older than Ben. Clara is younger than Ben. Dan is older than Clara but younger than Ben. Who is the second youngest?
questions.explanation: From oldest to youngest the order is Anna, Ben, Dan, Clara. Clara is the youngest, so Dan is the second youngest.
questions.hintText: Write the four names in a row from oldest to youngest.

questions.question: Mia, Noah and Olga each play a different instrument: piano, violin or drums. Mia does not play the piano. Noah plays neither the piano nor the violin. Who plays the violin?
questions.explanation: Noah plays neither piano nor violin, so he plays the drums. Mia does not play the piano, so she plays the violin, and Olga plays the piano.
questions.hintText: Start with the person who has only one instrument left.

questions.question: All roses are flowers. Some flowers fade quickly. Which conclusion must be true?
questions.optionsString: Some roses fade quickly|All roses fade quickly|No roses fade quickly|None of these is certain
questions.explanation: The flowers that fade quickly may or may not include roses, so nothing about roses follows. 'Some roses fade quickly' sounds plausible but is not guaranteed by the two statements.
questions.hintText: Draw circles for roses and flowers: where could the quickly fading flowers lie?

questions.question: What is the logical negation of the statement 'All students passed the test'?
questions.optionsString: At least one student failed|No student passed|Exactly one student failed|At least one student passed
questions.explanation: To disprove 'all passed' a single counterexample is enough, so the negation is 'at least one student failed'. 'No student passed' goes too far: it is the opposite extreme, not the negation.
questions.hintText: How many counterexamples do you need to show that an 'all' statement is false?
questions.acceptedAnswers: At least one student did not pass|Not all students passed|Some student failed

questions.question: A drawer holds many loose socks in 4 colours. In the dark, how many socks must you take to be sure of getting two of the same colour?
