questions.explanation: Earth takes about 365.25 days (one full year) to orbit the Sun once.
questions.hintText: How long until your birthday comes around again?

questions.question: Animals with backbones (spines) are called vertebrates. Which of these is an INVERTEBRATE (no bones)?
questions.explanation: Jellyfish have soft bodies with no skeleton or backbone (invertebrates).
questions.hintText: Think of which one is soft and wobbly all over, with nothing hard inside.

questions.question: Why do objects cast shadows on the ground on a sunny day?
questions.optionsString: Light goes straight and the object blocks it|The ground absorbs all the sunlight|The object gives off cold darkness|The Sun switches off behind it
questions.explanation: Light rays travel in straight lines. When an opaque object blocks the rays, an unlit shadow forms behind it.
questions.hintText: Hold your hand in front of a lamp: what does your hand do to the light?

questions.question: Which planet is nicknamed the 'Red Planet' because of its rusty iron-rich soil?
questions.explanation: Mars has abundant iron oxide (rust) on its surface, giving it a distinct reddish appearance.
questions.hintText: The 4th planet from the Sun.

questions.question: What do we call animals that eat ONLY plants (like rabbits and cows)?
questions.explanation: Herbivores (from Latin herba = plant) feed exclusively on plant matter.
questions.hintText: Look at the start of each word. One sounds like 'herb', a green plant.

questions.question: Why does the Moon appear to change shape (phases: crescent, half, full) from Earth?
questions.optionsString: The Moon physically grows and shrinks|We see different parts of its sunlit half|Earth's clouds cover parts of the Moon|The Sun turns off one side of the Moon
questions.explanation: As the Moon circles Earth, our viewpoint of the half illuminated by the Sun changes continually.
questions.hintText: Shine a lamp on a ball and walk around it. Does the lit part look the same?

questions.question: What do we call it when an animal blends into its surroundings (like a chameleon or arctic fox)?
questions.explanation: Camouflage allows animals to disguise their appearance to hide from predators or prey.
questions.hintText: Think of playing hide-and-seek in clothes that match the wall.

questions.question: Which of these materials is an ELECTRICAL CONDUCTOR (allows electricity to flow through it)?
questions.explanation: Metals like copper have free electrons and are excellent electrical conductors.
questions.hintText: Think of what a charger cable is made of inside, under its soft cover.

questions.question: What are fossils?
questions.optionsString: Rare rocks formed in space|Remains of ancient life kept in rock|Pieces of fallen meteorites|Frozen water underground
questions.explanation: Fossils are the mineralized remains of ancient plants, animals, or dinosaur bones preserved in stone.
questions.hintText: How scientists study dinosaurs that lived millions of years ago.

questions.question: Which habitat has very little rain, very hot days and cactus plants?
questions.explanation: Deserts get less than 25 cm of rain in a year. Plants like cacti store water so they can live there.
questions.hintText: Think of where a camel feels at home.

questions.question: How is sound created?
questions.optionsString: By very bright light|By very cold air|By something that vibrates|By strong magnets
questions.explanation: Sound is produced when a vibrating object causes pressure waves in the surrounding air, liquid, or solid.
questions.hintText: Put your fingers on your throat and hum. What do you feel?

questions.question: Which invisible force pulls rain, rivers, and all objects down to the ground?
questions.explanation: Gravity is the attractive force that Earth exerts on all masses.
questions.hintText: Jump as high as you can: what brings you back down?

questions.question: How many bones does an adult human body have?
questions.explanation: An adult human skeleton consists of 206 distinct bones.
questions.hintText: Babies have about 300 bones, but many join together as you grow up.
questions.acceptedAnswers: two hundred six|two hundred and six

questions.question: What is the green pigment in plant leaves that absorbs sunlight for photosynthesis?
questions.explanation: Chlorophyll absorbs red and blue light from the Sun and gives leaves their green color.
questions.hintText: Think of it as the plant's tiny solar panels.

questions.question: Which planet is famous for its massive, beautiful system of rings made of ice and rock particles?
questions.explanation: Saturn is the gas giant renowned for its spectacular, wide ring system.
questions.hintText: Count outward from the Sun: it is the 6th planet.

questions.question: What causes thunder during a thunderstorm?
questions.optionsString: Clouds crashing together like rocks|Lightning heats air so fast that it bursts outward|Rain falling too fast|Wind shaking the mountains
questions.explanation: Lightning heats the surrounding air channel to ~30,000 °C in milliseconds; the rapid explosive expansion creates thunder.
questions.hintText: A popping balloon makes a bang because air moves suddenly.

questions.question: How do bats navigate and find tiny insects in pitch darkness?
questions.optionsString: Echolocation (listening to echoes)|Seeing the heat of insects|Smelling insects from miles away|Following a built-in compass
questions.explanation: Bats use echolocation: high-frequency ultrasound calls bounce off targets and reveal their exact location.
questions.hintText: Shout in a big empty hall or tunnel: what comes back to your ears?

questions.question: What is molten liquid rock called while it is STILL underground inside a volcano?
questions.explanation: Underground it is called magma; once it erupts onto the surface it is called lava.
questions.hintText: Once it pours out into the open air, it gets a new name.

questions.question: What covers approximately 71% of the entire surface of planet Earth?
questions.explanation: Oceans cover roughly 71% of Earth's surface, which is why Earth is called the 'Blue Marble'.
questions.hintText: Spin a globe: which kind of area do you see most?

questions.question: What gas do humans and animals exhale into the air that green plants absorb?
questions.explanation: Animals breathe in O₂ and exhale CO₂; plants use CO₂ in photosynthesis to generate oxygen.
questions.hintText: You breathe this gas out, and fizzy drinks have it in their bubbles.

questions.question: Which animal has feathers?
questions.explanation: Ducks are birds, and all birds have feathers. Feathers keep them warm and dry.
questions.hintText: Feathers belong to birds. Which one is a bird?

questions.question: What does a caterpillar turn into when it is grown up?
questions.explanation: A caterpillar eats and grows, then rests inside a case. It comes out as a butterfly with wings.
questions.hintText: Think of the insect with big colourful wings in the garden.

questions.question: Which of these does a plant need to stay alive?
questions.explanation: Plants drink water through their roots. Without water they dry out and wilt.
questions.hintText: Think of what you pour on a flower pot when the soil is dry.

questions.question: Which sense tells you that a lemon is sour?
questions.explanation: Your tongue has tiny taste buds. They tell you if food is sour, sweet, salty or bitter.
questions.hintText: Which part of your body does the lemon juice touch when you eat it?

questions.question: How often should you brush your teeth?
questions.optionsString: Once a week|Twice a day|Once a month|Only when sore
questions.explanation: Brush in the morning and before bed. That clears away the germs that make holes in teeth.
questions.hintText: Think of the time after you wake up and the time before you go to bed.
questions.acceptedAnswers: 2 times a day|two times a day|morning and evening

questions.question: Why do we wash our hands with soap before eating?
questions.optionsString: To wash off germs|To cool them down|To make them soft|To help nails grow
questions.explanation: Tiny germs sit on your hands, too small to see. Soap and water wash them away, so they do not get into your food.
questions.hintText: Something too small to see sits on your hands and can make you ill.

questions.question: Which material can you see through clearly?
questions.explanation: Glass lets light pass through, so you can see what is behind it. That is why windows are made of glass.
questions.hintText: Think of what a window is made of.

questions.question: Which of these is a liquid?
questions.explanation: Juice flows and can be poured, so it is a liquid. A stone, a spoon and an ice cube are solids.
questions.hintText: A liquid can be poured from one cup into another.

questions.question: In which season do many trees drop their leaves?
questions.explanation: In autumn the days get shorter and cooler. Many trees drop their leaves and rest through the winter.
questions.hintText: The leaves turn yellow, red and brown first.

questions.question: What gives Earth its daylight and warmth?
questions.explanation: The Sun is a huge, very hot ball of glowing gas. Its light and heat reach Earth every day.
questions.hintText: It rises in the morning and sets in the evening.

questions.question: Which of these sounds is the quietest?
questions.explanation: A whisper is very soft, so you must be close to hear it. Drums, horns and thunder are loud.
questions.hintText: Which one do you use to tell a secret?

questions.question: Which object will a magnet pull towards itself?
questions.optionsString: A steel paper clip|A wooden pencil|A rubber band|A glass marble
questions.explanation: Magnets pull things made of iron or steel. Wood, rubber and glass are not pulled by a magnet.
questions.hintText: Look for the object made of metal.

questions.question: A ball is lying still on the grass. You kick it. What does your kick make it do?
questions.explanation: A kick is a push. A push or a pull can make a still thing start to move.
questions.hintText: A kick is a push. What does a push do to a toy car?
questions.acceptedAnswers: it moves|it starts to move|move|roll away

questions.question: Why should you never touch a light switch with wet hands?
questions.optionsString: The light would get dimmer|The switch would get dirty|The water would get hot|You could get an electric shock
questions.explanation: Water lets electricity pass through. With wet hands the electricity could reach your body, so dry your hands first.
questions.hintText: Water and electricity are a dangerous mix.
questions.acceptedAnswers: electric shock|a shock|you get a shock

questions.question: Into which bin should an old newspaper go?
questions.optionsString: Glass bin|Food waste bin|Paper bin|Battery box
questions.explanation: A newspaper is made of paper. Old paper can be turned into new paper and cardboard.
questions.hintText: Think of what a newspaper is made of.

questions.question: Which animal lives in the cold Arctic?
questions.explanation: Polar bears live on the ice of the Arctic. Thick fur and a layer of fat keep them warm.
questions.hintText: Its white fur matches the snow.

questions.question: Which organ do you use to think and remember?
questions.explanation: Your brain sits inside your head. It thinks, remembers and tells your body what to do.
questions.hintText: It is inside your head, kept safe by your skull.

questions.question: What falls from grey clouds as drops of water?
questions.explanation: Clouds are made of tiny drops of water. When the drops grow big and heavy, they fall as rain.
questions.hintText: You need an umbrella for it.

questions.question: Which of these animals lays eggs?
questions.explanation: A hen is a bird, and birds lay eggs. Cows, dogs and mice give birth to live babies.
questions.hintText: Think of where the eggs for breakfast come from.

questions.question: What do we call air that moves?
questions.explanation: Wind is moving air. You cannot see it, but you feel it on your face and see it shake the trees.
questions.hintText: It makes kites fly and leaves dance.

questions.question: Which of these is a living thing?
questions.explanation: A tree is alive: it grows, takes in water and makes seeds. Rocks, clouds and rivers are not alive.
questions.hintText: Living things grow and need food or water.

questions.question: Ice cream left in the sun turns soft and runny. What is this change called?
questions.explanation: Heat turns a solid into a liquid. This is called melting, and it happens to ice, butter and chocolate too.
questions.hintText: The same thing happens to a snowman on a warm day.

questions.question: Which of these animals is a mammal?
questions.explanation: A dolphin breathes air with lungs and feeds its baby with milk, so it is a mammal. A shark is a fish and a penguin is a bird.
questions.hintText: Mammals breathe air and feed their babies with milk.

questions.question: How many legs does an insect, such as an ant or a bee, have?
questions.explanation: Every insect has 6 legs, 3 on each side. Spiders have 8 legs, so they are not insects.
questions.hintText: Picture an ant: count the legs on one side, then double.

questions.question: A tadpole hatches from an egg in a pond. What does it grow into?
questions.explanation: A tadpole has a tail and lives in water. Slowly it grows legs, loses its tail and becomes a frog.
questions.hintText: It grows legs and loses its tail as it gets older.

questions.question: What do fish use to breathe under water?
questions.explanation: Fish have gills on the sides of their head. Gills take the oxygen out of the water.
questions.hintText: Look for the slits on the side of a fish's head.

questions.question: Hedgehogs sleep in a nest of leaves all through the cold winter. What is this long sleep called?
questions.explanation: In winter there is little food. Hedgehogs save energy by sleeping for months. This is called hibernation.
questions.hintText: It is a way to save energy when food is hard to find in winter.

questions.question: Which part of a plant makes the seeds?
questions.explanation: Seeds form inside the flower. Later the flower turns into a fruit with the seeds in it.
questions.hintText: It is the colourful part that bees like to visit.

questions.question: How do the fluffy seeds of a dandelion travel to new places?
questions.optionsString: By water|On animal fur|By wind|Inside birds
questions.explanation: Each dandelion seed has a tiny fluffy parachute. The wind lifts it and carries it far away.
questions.hintText: What happens when you blow on a dandelion clock?

questions.question: Which body parts pull on your bones to make you move?
questions.explanation: Muscles are joined to your bones. When a muscle gets shorter, it pulls the bone and your arm or leg moves.
questions.hintText: Bend your arm and feel what gets hard and thick above your elbow.

questions.question: Which organ mixes and breaks down the food you swallow?
questions.explanation: Food slides down a tube into your stomach. There it is mixed with juices and broken into tiny bits.
questions.hintText: It rumbles when you are hungry.

questions.question: About how long should a child of your age sleep each night?
questions.explanation: School children need about 9 to 11 hours of sleep. While you sleep, your body grows and your brain sorts what you learned.
questions.hintText: Count from an early bedtime to the time you get up for school.

questions.question: Is the air around us a solid, a liquid or a gas?
questions.optionsString: A gas|A liquid|A solid|Nothing at all
questions.explanation: Air is a mix of gases. You cannot see it, but it fills a balloon and you feel it as wind.
questions.hintText: It spreads out to fill any space, like the inside of a balloon.

questions.question: You pour juice from a tall glass into a wide bowl. What happens to the juice?
questions.optionsString: It turns into a gas|It keeps its tall shape|It gets heavier|It takes the bowl's shape
questions.explanation: A liquid has no shape of its own. It always takes the shape of the cup or bowl that holds it.
questions.hintText: Think about how water looks in a bottle, a cup and a puddle.

questions.question: What are clouds made of?
questions.optionsString: Smoke from fires|Tiny drops of water|Fine white dust|Thick warm air
questions.explanation: Warm, wet air rises and cools. The water in it turns into tiny drops, and millions of them make a cloud.
questions.hintText: Think of the mist you see when you breathe out on a cold day.

questions.question: Which tool measures how warm or cold the air is?
questions.explanation: A thermometer shows the temperature in degrees. A high number means warm, a low number means cold.
questions.hintText: A doctor uses a small one to check if you have a fever.

questions.question: Why do we have day and night?
questions.optionsString: The Sun circles Earth|The Moon hides the Sun|Earth spins like a top|Clouds cover the Sun
questions.explanation: Earth spins around once every 24 hours. The side facing the Sun has day, and the other side has night.
questions.hintText: Shine a torch on a ball and slowly turn the ball.
questions.acceptedAnswers: Earth spins|the Earth spins|Earth turns|Earth rotates

questions.question: In which direction does the Sun rise in the morning?
questions.explanation: Earth spins towards the east, so we see the Sun come up in the east. In the evening it sets in the west.
questions.hintText: It is the opposite of where the Sun sets in the evening.

questions.question: What is the Sun?
questions.explanation: The Sun is a star, a giant ball of glowing hot gas. It looks bigger than other stars because it is much closer to us.
questions.hintText: It makes its own light, like the tiny lights in the night sky.

questions.question: You shout in a mountain valley and hear your voice come back. What is this called?
questions.explanation: Sound bounces off hard walls like rock. The sound that comes back to your ears is an echo.
questions.hintText: Sound can bounce off a hard wall, like a ball.

questions.question: On which floor will a toy car roll the farthest after the same push?
questions.explanation: A smooth floor rubs against the wheels only a little. Rough carpet, grass and sand rub more and slow the car sooner.
questions.hintText: Rough ground rubs against the wheels and slows them down.

questions.question: A battery, wires and a bulb make a loop, and the bulb glows. What happens if one wire comes loose?
questions.optionsString: The bulb gets brighter|The bulb starts to blink|The battery fills up|The bulb goes out
questions.explanation: Electricity flows only around a complete loop. A loose wire breaks the loop, so the bulb goes out.
questions.hintText: Electricity needs an unbroken path all the way around.
questions.acceptedAnswers: it goes out|the light goes out|it turns off

questions.question: Fruit peels and old leaves rot in a compost heap. What do they turn into?
questions.explanation: Worms and tiny living things eat the peels and leaves. They turn them into dark, rich soil that feeds new plants.
questions.hintText: Gardeners spread it on their beds to help plants grow.

questions.question: Which of these small animals is NOT an insect?
questions.explanation: Insects have 6 legs. A spider has 8 legs and no wings, so it belongs to a different group.
questions.hintText: Count the legs: an insect always has six.

questions.question: A frog starts life in water and later lives on land too. Which animal group is it in?
questions.explanation: Amphibians such as frogs and newts begin life in water and later breathe air on land. Their skin is soft and moist.
questions.hintText: Its skin is soft and wet, not dry and scaly like a lizard's.

questions.question: A butterfly's life has four stages. Which stage comes right after the caterpillar?
questions.explanation: The order is egg, caterpillar, chrysalis, butterfly. Inside the chrysalis the caterpillar slowly changes into a butterfly.
questions.hintText: The caterpillar hangs still inside a hard case before it gets wings.

questions.question: Bees carry pollen from flower to flower so that seeds can form. What is this called?
questions.explanation: Pollen is a fine yellow powder made by flowers. When it reaches another flower, that flower can make seeds. This is pollination.
questions.hintText: Without this step an apple tree would grow no apples.

questions.question: What does almost every food chain start with?
questions.optionsString: A meat eater|A plant eater|A green plant|A small insect
questions.explanation: Green plants make their own food from sunlight. Animals cannot do this, so a food chain begins with a plant, such as grass → rabbit → fox.
questions.hintText: Who can make food from sunlight without eating anything?

questions.question: What is stored inside a camel's hump?
questions.explanation: The hump is a store of fat. The camel uses this fat as food when it finds nothing to eat in the desert. It is not a water tank.
questions.hintText: The hump gets smaller when the camel has had nothing to eat for a long time.

questions.question: Swallows fly to warm lands every autumn and come back in spring. What is this journey called?
questions.explanation: In winter swallows find no insects to eat here. So they fly far south and return in spring. This yearly journey is called migration.
questions.hintText: It is a long trip that the birds repeat every single year.

questions.question: What carries messages between your brain and the rest of your body?
questions.explanation: Nerves are like thin wires that run through your whole body. They carry signals to and from your brain very fast.
questions.hintText: They work like tiny telephone wires inside you.

questions.question: Milk and cheese give your body calcium. What does your body need calcium for most of all?
questions.optionsString: For shiny hair|For sharp eyes|For strong bones|For soft skin
questions.explanation: Calcium makes bones and teeth hard. Milk, cheese and yoghurt give you plenty of it while you grow.
questions.hintText: Think of the hardest parts inside your body.
questions.acceptedAnswers: bones|strong bones|bones and teeth|strong bones and teeth|teeth

questions.question: Which of these changes can NOT be undone?
questions.optionsString: Frying an egg|Melting ice|Freezing juice|Melting chocolate
questions.explanation: Ice, juice and chocolate can be frozen and melted again and again. A fried egg can never become a raw egg again.
questions.hintText: Ask for each one: can I get the first thing back by cooling or warming it?

questions.question: You stir a spoon of sugar into warm water and it seems to vanish. What happened to the sugar?
questions.explanation: The sugar broke into bits too small to see and spread through the water. It is still there: the water tastes sweet. This is called dissolving.
questions.hintText: Taste the water: the sugar is still in there, mixed in.

questions.question: On a xylophone, which bars make the highest notes?
questions.optionsString: The longest bars|The widest bars|The middle bars|The shortest bars
questions.explanation: A short bar shakes back and forth very quickly, and fast shaking makes a high note. Long bars shake slowly and sound low.
questions.hintText: Small things usually shake faster than big things.

questions.question: On a cold day, tiny drops of water form on the inside of a window. What is this called?
questions.explanation: Warm air in the room holds invisible water vapour. When it touches the cold glass, it cools and turns back into drops of water. This is condensation.
questions.hintText: It is the opposite of a puddle drying up in the sun.

questions.question: What kind of water is most of the water on Earth?
questions.optionsString: Salty sea water|Fresh river water|Rain water|Water in lakes
questions.explanation: Almost all of Earth's water is in the salty seas and oceans. Only a small part is fresh water that we can drink.
questions.hintText: Look at a globe and find where the biggest blue areas are.

questions.question: What is fog?
questions.optionsString: Smoke from chimneys|Very fine snow|Dust in the wind|A cloud near the ground
questions.explanation: Fog is made of tiny drops of water floating in the air, just like a cloud. The only difference is that it touches the ground.
questions.hintText: Think of what you would walk through on top of a very high mountain.
questions.acceptedAnswers: a cloud|a low cloud|cloud on the ground

questions.question: Why do you see lightning before you hear its thunder?
questions.optionsString: Thunder starts later|Light is faster than sound|Sound is faster than light|Clouds slow the sound
questions.explanation: Lightning and thunder happen at the same moment. Light reaches you almost at once, but sound travels much more slowly, so the thunder arrives later.
questions.hintText: Both start together, but they travel to you at different speeds.
questions.acceptedAnswers: light travels faster than sound|light is faster

questions.question: About how long does the Moon take to travel once around Earth?
questions.explanation: The Moon needs about 27 days to circle Earth, which is close to one month. The word 'month' even comes from 'Moon'.
questions.hintText: Count the days from one full Moon to the next.
questions.acceptedAnswers: 1 month|one month|a month|about a month|27 days

questions.question: Which planet is the closest to the Sun?
questions.explanation: Mercury is the first planet from the Sun. Then come Venus, Earth and Mars.
questions.hintText: It races around the Sun faster than any other planet.

questions.question: The Moon does not make its own light. Why does it shine at night?
questions.optionsString: It glows from heat inside|It burns like a candle|Stars light it up|It reflects sunlight
questions.explanation: The Moon is a ball of rock. Sunlight falls on it and bounces off towards Earth, like light from a mirror.
questions.hintText: Think of how a white wall looks bright when a torch shines on it.
questions.acceptedAnswers: it reflects the Sun's light|sunlight bounces off it|reflects sunlight

questions.question: At what time on a sunny day is your shadow the shortest?
questions.optionsString: At sunrise|At midday|In late afternoon|At sunset
questions.explanation: At midday the Sun is at its highest point in the sky. Light then comes from high above, so your shadow is short.
questions.hintText: A lamp held high above a toy makes a small shadow. When is the Sun highest?

questions.question: You move your hand closer to a lamp. What happens to its shadow on the wall?
questions.optionsString: It gets smaller|It disappears|It gets bigger|It stays the same
questions.explanation: Near the lamp your hand blocks more of the light that spreads out from it. So the shadow on the wall grows.
questions.hintText: Close to the lamp, your hand stands in the way of more light.

questions.question: A parachute falls slowly and gently. What pushes up against it and slows it down?
questions.explanation: The wide parachute has to push a lot of air out of its way. The air pushes back and slows the fall. This push is called air resistance.
questions.hintText: Run with a big open umbrella: what do you feel pushing against it?

questions.question: Not every metal sticks to a magnet. Which of these metals does a magnet attract?
questions.explanation: Magnets attract iron and things that contain iron, such as steel. Aluminium, copper and gold are metals too, but a magnet does not pull them.
questions.hintText: Steel nails and paper clips are made mostly of this metal.

questions.question: Why is the metal wire in a cable covered with plastic?
questions.optionsString: To make the wire stronger|To keep the wire warm|To keep the electricity in|To make the cable lighter
questions.explanation: Electricity flows easily through metal but not through plastic. The plastic cover keeps the electricity inside the wire, so you can touch the cable safely.
questions.hintText: Electricity can pass through metal, but not through this cover.

packs.title: Junior Chess, Word Heroes & Kid Coding (7–9 yrs)
packs.subtitle: 1-move Junior Chess mates on the 2D board, vocabulary opposites & robot repeat loops
packs.author: Kmito Junior Academy

questions.question: White to move: The Black King on g8 is trapped behind its own pawns! Find Checkmate in 1 move!
questions.explanation: 1. Ra8# is the classic Back-Rank Mate! Black's own pawns on f7, g7, and h7 block the King from escaping.
questions.hintText: Your rook can zoom to the back row. Look at where the Black King is stuck!

questions.question: White to move: Use your Queen and King to deliver Checkmate in 1 move!
questions.explanation: 1. Qa8# is mate! The Queen checks along the top row and covers e8 and g8, while the White King on f6 guards e7, f7 and g7.
questions.hintText: Your Queen can reach the top row. Your King already guards the squares next to Black's King.

questions.question: Which word is the OPPOSITE (antonym) of 'ANCIENT' (very, very old)?
questions.explanation: 'Ancient' means from a very long time ago, so its opposite (antonym) is 'Modern' (new, from today).
questions.hintText: Ancient pyramids are old; today's cities are...

questions.question: If a turtle walks at a 'SLUGGISH' pace, how is the turtle moving?
questions.optionsString: Very slowly|Super fast|Backwards|High in the sky
questions.explanation: 'Sluggish' (like a garden slug!) means moving very slowly and with low energy.
questions.hintText: Think of how fast a little slug or snail moves!

questions.question: You program a toy robot with the block: [REPEAT 4 TIMES: Jump 3 steps forward]. How many steps does the robot jump in total?
questions.explanation: A repeat loop runs the instruction 4 times: 3 + 3 + 3 + 3 = 4 × 3 = 12 steps forward!
questions.hintText: Picture 4 jumps in a row and add up the steps of every jump.

questions.question: Your robot faces NORTH. You run: [Turn Right 90°] then [Turn Right 90°] again. Which direction is the robot facing now?
questions.explanation: Facing North → Turn Right once faces East (90°) → Turn Right a second time faces South (180° opposite)!
questions.hintText: Draw a compass. Turn right once, then once more.

questions.question: In standard chess valuation, how many points is a Rook worth?
questions.explanation: Pawn = 1, Knight/Bishop = 3, Rook = 5, Queen = 9.
questions.hintText: A pawn is worth 1. A rook is stronger than a bishop but weaker than a queen.

questions.question: Which word means the same as 'GIGANTIC'?
questions.explanation: 'Gigantic' and 'Enormous' both describe something exceptionally huge.
questions.hintText: The word starts like 'giant'. How big is a giant?

questions.question: Your robot is at square (0, 0). It executes [MOVE FORWARD 2], then [MOVE FORWARD 3]. How many squares did it move?
questions.explanation: 2 + 3 = 5 squares total.
questions.hintText: Both moves go the same way, so put them together.

questions.question: Which piece moves in an 'L-shape' (two squares one way, then one square perpendicular) and can jump over other pieces?
questions.explanation: The Knight moves in an L-shape and is the only piece that can jump over others.
questions.hintText: Shaped like a horse.

questions.question: What is the direct antonym (opposite) of 'BRAVE'?
questions.explanation: The opposite of brave is cowardly (fearful).
questions.hintText: A hero is brave; someone who runs away in fear is...

questions.question: In code, if a statement says `IF is_raining == True: take_umbrella() ELSE: wear_sunglasses()`. If it is SUNNY outside, what do you do?
questions.explanation: Since is_raining is False, the code enters the ELSE block: wear_sunglasses().
questions.hintText: On a sunny day, is 'is_raining' true or false? Then see which part of the code runs.

questions.question: What do we call a double attack where one piece, often a Knight, attacks TWO enemy pieces at once?
questions.explanation: A fork is a tactical maneuver where a single piece (often a Knight) attacks two enemy pieces at once.
questions.hintText: Think of a tool for eating at dinner: it has several points that poke at once.

questions.question: Which of these words is made of TWO words joined together?
questions.explanation: Butterfly is formed from 'butter' and 'fly'.
questions.hintText: Find a word you can split into two smaller words you already know.

questions.question: A drawing program repeats: [DRAW LINE, TURN 45°] 8 times. What shape does it draw?
questions.explanation: 8 sides × 45° = 360°, forming a complete 8-sided regular Octagon.
questions.hintText: 8 repetitions create an 8-sided shape.

questions.question: How many total squares are on a standard 8×8 chessboard?
questions.explanation: 8 rows × 8 columns = 64 squares (32 light and 32 dark).
questions.hintText: Count by 8s once for each row of the board.

questions.question: What is an antonym for 'FREEZE'?
questions.explanation: The opposite of freeze is melt.
questions.hintText: Ice freezes; when it gets warm, it...

questions.question: You store `apples = 5`. Then you execute `apples = apples + 3`. What is the value stored in apples now?
questions.hintText: Picture a basket with 5 apples. The code puts in 3 more. Count them all.

questions.question: What is a 'PIN' in chess?
questions.optionsString: A piece that cannot move without exposing a bigger piece|Two pawns bump into each other head on and block the way|A pawn that reaches the last row and becomes a Queen|Moving two knights at the same time in a single turn
questions.explanation: A pin prevents an enemy piece from moving because doing so would expose the King or Queen behind it.
questions.hintText: Think of a pin holding paper on a wall: it can't wiggle away.

questions.question: What does 'SWIFT' mean?
questions.explanation: 'Swift' means moving or capable of moving with great speed.
questions.hintText: A swift runner is the first to cross the finish line.

questions.question: A bug in computer programming is:
questions.optionsString: A mistake in a program's code|A real beetle in the keyboard|A trick that makes games faster|A new kind of computer mouse
questions.explanation: A bug is an unintentional coding flaw or logic error in software.
questions.hintText: Programmers 'debug' their code. What are they looking for and fixing?

questions.question: Can a King EVER move to a square attacked by an enemy piece?
questions.optionsString: Yes, but only if it has no other move|No, never: that is moving into check|Yes, but only on the first move of the game|Only if it is capturing a Queen
questions.explanation: Moving the King into check is strictly illegal in chess.
questions.hintText: What would happen if your King stood on a square an enemy piece attacks?

questions.question: The prefix 'TELE-' (in telephone, telescope, television) comes from Greek and means:
questions.explanation: Greek 'tele' means far or distant (seeing far, hearing far).
questions.hintText: A telephone lets you talk to a friend who is not in the same room.

questions.question: To make a sandwich, which step MUST come first?
questions.optionsString: Eat the sandwich|Take two slices of bread|Put the plate in the dishwasher|Wrap the sandwich in foil
questions.explanation: Algorithms require strict logical order: you must get the bread before making the sandwich.
questions.hintText: Think of the steps in order. Which one needs nothing before it?

questions.question: What special pawn capture can ONLY happen immediately after an enemy pawn moves two squares forward from its starting rank?
questions.explanation: En Passant allows a pawn to capture an adjacent enemy pawn that just moved two squares past it.
questions.hintText: It has a French name. Your pawn captures as if the enemy pawn moved only one step.

questions.question: A comparison that uses the words 'like' or 'as' (e.g. 'brave as a lion') is called a:
questions.explanation: A simile compares two things using 'like' or 'as'.
questions.hintText: Think of the word 'similar': the two things are alike.

questions.question: `count = 0; REPEAT 4 TIMES: count = count + 2`. What is count at the end?
questions.explanation: 4 repetitions × 2 = 8.
questions.hintText: Start at 0 and count up in 2s, once for every repeat.

questions.question: A 'SKEWER' is like a reverse pin: which piece is attacked in FRONT?
questions.optionsString: A pawn, with a Queen standing behind it|A piece that is worth less than the piece behind it|A piece that is worth more than the piece behind it|A piece that is worth exactly the same as the one behind
questions.explanation: In a skewer, the more valuable piece (e.g. King or Queen) is in front and is forced to move, exposing a piece behind.
questions.hintText: Picture a kebab stick going through two pieces in a line.

questions.question: What does the popular idiom 'A piece of cake' mean?
questions.optionsString: A tasty dessert from a bakery|Something that is very easy to do|A very hard homework task|An expensive birthday present
questions.explanation: 'A piece of cake' is an English idiom meaning an effortless, very easy task.
questions.hintText: It isn't about food. Think of a job you can do without any trouble.

questions.question: A robot starts facing East. Which command turns it to face North?
questions.optionsString: Turn Left 90°|Turn Right 90°|Turn Around 180°|Move Forward 1 step
questions.explanation: Facing East (right), turning counter-clockwise (Left 90°) points directly to North (up).
questions.hintText: Draw a compass: East is on the right and North is at the top. Which way do you turn?

questions.question: What is STALEMATE in chess?
questions.optionsString: The King is in check and has no escape (a loss)|A player has no legal move and is NOT in check (a draw)|A pawn is promoted to a Knight on the last row|A player's time on the clock runs out
questions.explanation: Stalemate occurs when the player to move has no legal moves and their King is NOT in check; the game ends in an immediate DRAW.
questions.hintText: Ask two questions: is the King attacked, and can any piece move?

questions.question: Which word is an ADJECTIVE (describes a noun)?
questions.explanation: 'Playful' is an adjective (e.g. a playful puppy). 'Play' is a verb, 'Quickly' an adverb, 'Player' a noun.
questions.hintText: Which word fits in 'The ___ puppy ran home'?

questions.question: Computers store all photos, sounds, and games using binary digits (bits). What TWO numbers make up binary?
questions.explanation: Binary code is base-2, using only the digits 0 and 1 (off and on).
questions.hintText: Think of a light switch: it has only two settings.

questions.question: White to move: Your two Rooks work as a team. Find checkmate in 1 move!
questions.explanation: 1. Rb8 is checkmate! One Rook guards the 7th row, so the King cannot step forward. The other Rook checks on the 8th row.
questions.hintText: One Rook already blocks a row. Use the other Rook to attack the King's row.

questions.question: White to move: The Black King is stuck on the edge of the board. Find checkmate in 1 move!
questions.explanation: 1. Rh1 is checkmate! The Rook attacks the whole h-file, and your King guards g3, g4 and g5.
questions.hintText: Your King already guards the squares beside the Black King. Attack the edge line with your Rook.

questions.question: White to move: Your Bishop is aiming far across the board. Find checkmate in 1 move!
questions.explanation: 1. Qxg7 is checkmate! The Queen lands right next to the King, and the Bishop on b2 protects her, so the King cannot capture.
questions.hintText: A Queen next to the King is safe when a friend protects her. Follow the Bishop's diagonal.

questions.question: White to move: The Black King is boxed in by its own pieces. Find checkmate in 1 move!
questions.explanation: 1. Nf7 is checkmate! The Knight gives check, and the King has no free square: its own Rook and pawns stand in the way.
questions.hintText: The King has no room to move. Which piece can jump in and give check?

questions.question: White to move: Two Bishops and the King have trapped the Black King. Find checkmate in 1 move!
questions.explanation: 1. Bb2 is checkmate! This Bishop checks along the long diagonal. The other Bishop guards g8, and your King guards g7 and h7.
questions.hintText: The King sits in a dark corner. Which Bishop can travel on dark squares?

questions.question: White to move: Your Queen and Knight attack together. Find checkmate in 1 move!
questions.explanation: 1. Qh7 is checkmate! The Knight on g5 protects the Queen, so the King cannot capture her. Black's own Rook and pawns block every escape.
questions.hintText: Find a square next to the King that your Knight already protects.

questions.question: White to move: Even the smallest piece can win the game. Find checkmate in 1 move!
questions.explanation: 1. g7 is checkmate! The pawn checks the King. Your King protects the pawn and guards h7, and the Bishop guards g8.
questions.hintText: Your King and Bishop already guard the escape squares. Who can give the check?

questions.question: Which chess piece moves only diagonally, as far as it likes?
questions.explanation: The Bishop slides along diagonals, as far as the way is free. That is why each Bishop always stays on squares of one color.
questions.hintText: This piece starts the game next to the King or the Queen.

questions.question: Which piece moves in straight lines, forward, backward and sideways, but never diagonally?
questions.explanation: The Rook moves straight along rows and columns, as far as the way is free. It never moves diagonally.
questions.hintText: This piece starts the game in a corner of the board.

questions.question: How many squares can the King move in one normal move?
questions.explanation: The King moves just 1 square at a time, in any direction. He is important, but slow!
questions.hintText: The King takes small steps, but he may go in any direction.

questions.question: How many pawns does each player have at the start of a chess game?
questions.explanation: Each player starts with 8 pawns. They stand in a row in front of the other pieces.
questions.hintText: The pawns fill one whole row of the board.

questions.question: Which side always makes the first move in a chess game?
questions.explanation: White always moves first. After that, the players take turns.
questions.hintText: Think of the two colors of the pieces. One of them always starts.

questions.question: How does a pawn capture an enemy piece?
questions.optionsString: One square diagonally forward|One square straight forward|One square to the side|Two squares straight forward
questions.explanation: A pawn moves straight ahead, but it captures one square diagonally forward. It is the only piece that captures differently from how it moves.
questions.hintText: A pawn does not capture the same way it moves.

questions.question: The Queen moves like two other pieces put together. Which two?
questions.optionsString: Rook and Knight|Rook and Bishop|Bishop and Knight|King and Knight
questions.explanation: The Queen can move straight like a Rook and diagonally like a Bishop. That makes her the strongest piece.
questions.hintText: The Queen goes straight and diagonally, but she cannot jump.

questions.question: Castling is a special move. Which two pieces move at the same time?
questions.optionsString: King and Queen|Rook and Bishop|King and Rook|Queen and Rook
questions.explanation: In castling, the King moves two squares toward a Rook, and that Rook jumps over to the King's other side. It keeps the King safe.
questions.hintText: One of the two pieces must be kept safe all game long. The other starts in a corner.

questions.question: How many points are a Rook and a Knight worth together?
questions.explanation: A Rook is worth 5 points and a Knight is worth 3 points. Together: 5 + 3 = 8 points.
questions.hintText: A Rook is worth 5 points. Find the Knight's points and add them.

questions.question: Your King is in check. Which of these is NOT a way to get out of check?
questions.optionsString: Skip your turn|Move the King away|Block the attack|Capture the attacker
questions.explanation: You can escape check in three ways: move the King, block the attack, or capture the attacking piece. You may never skip a turn in chess.
questions.hintText: Three of these are real ways to save the King. One is not allowed in chess at all.

questions.question: In chess notation, what does the move 'Nf3' mean?
questions.optionsString: A King moves to f3|A Knight moves to f3|A pawn moves to f3|A Bishop moves to f3
questions.explanation: The letter N stands for Knight, because K is already used for the King. So 'Nf3' means a Knight moves to the square f3.
questions.hintText: The letter K is already taken by the King, so another piece uses its second letter.

questions.question: A White Bishop stands on c1 on an empty board. Which square can it reach in one move?
questions.explanation: A Bishop moves diagonally. From c1 it slides to b2 and then a3. The squares c3, b1 and d3 are not on its diagonals.
questions.hintText: Follow the diagonals from c1: go one column sideways and one row up each time.

questions.question: You capture a Queen, but you lose a Rook and a Bishop for it. Who won more points?
questions.optionsString: Your opponent, by 1 point|Nobody, it is equal|Your opponent, by 2 points|You, by 1 point
questions.explanation: A Queen is worth 9 points. A Rook and a Bishop are worth 5 + 3 = 8 points. You won 9 and lost 8, so you are 1 point ahead.
questions.hintText: Add up the points of the pieces you lost. Compare them with the Queen's points.

questions.question: When are you NOT allowed to castle?
questions.optionsString: When your King is in check|When you have lost a pawn|When your Queen has moved|When your Bishop has moved
questions.explanation: You may not castle while your King is in check. You also may not castle if the King or that Rook has already moved.
questions.hintText: Castling is not an emergency exit for the King.

questions.question: A Black Rook stands alone on e8. Which of these squares is safe from it?
questions.explanation: A Rook attacks its whole row and its whole column. e4 is on the e-file, and a8 and h8 are on the 8th row. Only d7 is on neither line, so it is safe.
questions.hintText: Check each square: is it in the Rook's column (e) or in its row (8)?

questions.question: A Knight stands on the corner square a1. How many squares can it jump to?
questions.explanation: From the corner a1, the Knight can only jump to b3 or c2. That is 2 squares. A Knight in the corner is weak, so keep it near the middle!
questions.hintText: Try each L-shaped jump from the corner. Most of them land off the board.

questions.question: Which word is the OPPOSITE of 'EMPTY'?
questions.explanation: An empty glass has nothing in it. A full glass has no more room. So 'full' is the opposite of 'empty'.
questions.hintText: Picture a glass with nothing in it. Now pour in juice up to the top.

questions.question: Which word does NOT belong with the others?
questions.explanation: Apple, banana and pear are fruits. A carrot is a vegetable, so it does not belong.
questions.hintText: Three of these are the same kind of food. Find the name of their group first.

questions.question: Which word means almost the same as 'HAPPY'?
questions.explanation: 'Happy' and 'glad' both mean that you feel good and pleased.
questions.hintText: Think of how you feel when a friend comes to play.

questions.question: Which word fits best? 'The soup is too ___ to eat. I must blow on it.'
questions.explanation: We blow on food to cool it down. So the soup is too hot.
questions.hintText: Why do people blow on a spoon of soup?

questions.question: A hammer, a saw and a screwdriver are all kinds of...
questions.explanation: We use a hammer, a saw and a screwdriver to build and fix things. Things we work with are called tools.
questions.hintText: What do people use these three things for?

questions.question: Which word is the OPPOSITE of 'BEGIN'?
questions.explanation: To begin is to start something. To finish is to come to the end of it. 'Start' means the same as 'begin', not the opposite.
questions.hintText: A game begins. What happens when the time is up?

questions.question: Which word means almost the same as 'DIFFICULT'?
questions.explanation: A difficult puzzle is a hard puzzle. 'Easy' is the opposite.
questions.hintText: Think of a puzzle that takes you a long time to solve.

questions.question: What does an 'HONEST' person do?
questions.optionsString: Always comes first|Never feels tired|Always tells the truth|Never eats sweets
questions.explanation: An honest person tells the truth and does not cheat. People can trust them.
questions.hintText: Think of a friend you can always believe.

questions.question: Three of these words are about loud voices. Which one does NOT fit?
questions.explanation: Shout, yell and scream all mean to use a very loud voice. To whisper is to speak very quietly.
questions.hintText: Say each word the way it sounds. Which one would not wake a sleeping cat?

questions.question: Which word fits best? 'After the long race, Mia was so ___ that she fell asleep at once.'
questions.explanation: 'Exhausted' means very, very tired. After a long race your body needs rest.
questions.hintText: How does your body feel after you run for a long time?

questions.question: Which word is the OPPOSITE of 'WIDE'?
questions.explanation: A wide road has lots of room from side to side. A narrow road has very little. So 'narrow' is the opposite of 'wide'.
questions.hintText: Think of a big river and a tiny stream you can step across.

questions.question: If you are 'CURIOUS' about something, what do you want?
questions.optionsString: To go to sleep|To eat a snack|To know more|To be alone
questions.explanation: A curious person wants to find out more. Curious children ask lots of questions!
questions.hintText: Think of a child who keeps asking 'Why?'
questions.acceptedAnswers: To find out more|To learn more

questions.question: Which word is the group name for chair, table and bed?
questions.explanation: Chairs, tables and beds are things we put in rooms to sit, eat and sleep on. Together they are called furniture.
questions.hintText: These things stand in the rooms of a home.

questions.question: Which word is the OPPOSITE of 'ALWAYS'?
questions.explanation: 'Always' means every single time. 'Never' means not even one time. They are opposites.
questions.hintText: 'Always' means every single time. Look for the word that is as far from that as possible.

questions.question: Which word is the OPPOSITE of 'GENEROUS'?
questions.explanation: A generous person loves to share and give. A greedy person wants to keep everything. So 'greedy' is the opposite.
questions.hintText: A generous child shares the sweets. What do we call a child who keeps them all?

questions.question: A 'RARE' bird is a bird that...
questions.optionsString: Sings very loudly|Flies very high|Is not seen often|Eats only seeds
questions.explanation: 'Rare' means there are only a few, so you do not see it often. The opposite is 'common'.
questions.hintText: Bird watchers get very excited about a rare bird. Why might that be?

questions.question: Which word fits best? 'Grandma's old photo is very ___ to her. She keeps it in a safe place.'
questions.explanation: Something precious is very special and important to you. That is why Grandma keeps the photo safe.
questions.hintText: Why would someone keep a thing in a safe place?

questions.question: Which of these words is NOT a kind of weather?
questions.explanation: Drizzle is light rain, hail is balls of ice, and fog is a cloud near the ground. A shadow is just a dark shape where light is blocked.
questions.hintText: Three of these come from the sky or the air. One needs only a light and an object.

questions.question: What does it mean 'to OBSERVE' an animal?
questions.optionsString: To feed it well|To watch it carefully|To give it a name|To chase it away
questions.explanation: To observe means to watch something carefully and notice details. Scientists observe animals to learn how they live.
questions.hintText: Scientists do this quietly, often with binoculars and a notebook.
questions.acceptedAnswers: To watch it|To look at it carefully

questions.question: Which of these words means the COLDEST?
questions.explanation: The words go from a little cold to very cold: cool, chilly, cold, freezing. 'Freezing' is so cold that water turns to ice.
questions.hintText: Put the four words in order, from a fresh breeze to an icy winter night.

questions.question: Which word means almost the same as 'JOURNEY'?
questions.explanation: A journey is when you travel from one place to another. 'Trip' means the same. A map, a road and a ticket only help you on the way.
questions.hintText: It is the travelling itself, not a thing you take with you.

questions.question: A page is a part of a book. In the same way, a branch is a part of a...
questions.explanation: A book is made of pages, and a tree is made of branches, a trunk and roots. A leaf is smaller than a branch, and a forest is many trees.
questions.hintText: Look for the bigger thing that a branch belongs to, just as a page belongs to a book.

questions.question: You brush your teeth. Which step comes LAST?
questions.optionsString: Put paste on the brush|Rinse your mouth|Pick up the brush|Open the toothpaste
questions.explanation: First you open the toothpaste, pick up the brush and put paste on it. Then you brush. Rinsing your mouth comes at the very end.
questions.hintText: Act out the steps in your head, one after another.

questions.question: A robot gets the block [REPEAT 3 TIMES: Clap]. How many times does it clap?
questions.explanation: 'Repeat 3 times' means: do the same thing 3 times. Clap, clap, clap!
questions.hintText: The number in the block tells you how often the action happens.

questions.question: A robot's program is: 1. Stand up. 2. Jump. 3. Sit down. What does the robot do SECOND?
questions.explanation: A robot follows the steps in order: first stand up, second jump, third sit down. So the second action is the jump.
questions.hintText: A computer reads the steps from top to bottom, one at a time.

questions.question: The robot car has one rule: IF the light is red, THEN stop. The light is red. What does it do?
questions.optionsString: It stops|It drives on|It speeds up|It turns back
questions.explanation: The rule checks: is the light red? Yes, it is. So the THEN part happens, and the car stops.
questions.hintText: First check if the IF part is true. Then do what comes after THEN.

questions.question: What do we call a list of steps that tells a computer what to do?
questions.explanation: A program is a list of steps written for a computer. The computer follows them one by one.
questions.hintText: Games and apps are made of these lists of steps.

questions.question: A recipe has a bug. 1. Drink the cocoa. 2. Pour the milk. 3. Add cocoa powder. Which step is out of place?
questions.explanation: You cannot drink the cocoa before you make it! Step 1 must move to the end: pour the milk, add the powder, then drink.
questions.hintText: Try to follow the recipe exactly as written. Where do you get stuck?
questions.acceptedAnswers: The first step|First step|Drink the cocoa

questions.question: The program [Hop] [Hop] [Hop] [Hop] is long. Which block does the same job?
questions.optionsString: REPEAT 2 TIMES: Hop|REPEAT 3 TIMES: Hop|REPEAT 5 TIMES: Hop|REPEAT 4 TIMES: Hop
questions.explanation: The program says Hop 4 times. A loop can say that in one short block: REPEAT 4 TIMES: Hop.
questions.hintText: Count how many times the same command appears.

questions.question: A robot runs [REPEAT 2 TIMES: Beep, Flash]. What happens, in order?
questions.optionsString: Beep, Flash, Beep, Flash|Beep, Beep, Flash, Flash|Flash, Beep, Flash, Beep|Beep, Flash, Flash, Beep
questions.explanation: A loop does everything inside it, then starts again from the top. So: Beep, Flash, and then again Beep, Flash.
questions.hintText: Do the whole list inside the block once. Then do the whole list again.

questions.question: IF the number is bigger than 5, say 'Big'. ELSE say 'Small'. The number is 3. What does the program say?
questions.explanation: Is 3 bigger than 5? No. So the IF part is skipped and the ELSE part runs: the program says 'Small'.
questions.hintText: Check the IF question first: is it true or false for this number?

questions.question: A = put on shoes, B = put on socks, C = tie the laces. Which order works?
questions.optionsString: A, B, C|C, B, A|B, A, C|A, C, B
questions.explanation: Socks go on first (B), then the shoes (A), and you tie the laces last (C). In a program, the order of steps matters too.
questions.hintText: Which thing touches your foot first? Which step needs the shoe to be on already?

questions.question: In coding, what is a 'loop'?
questions.optionsString: Steps that are skipped|A very fast computer|A mistake in the code|Steps that repeat
questions.explanation: A loop tells the computer to do the same steps again and again. It saves you from writing them many times.
questions.hintText: Think of running laps around a track: the same path, again and again.

questions.question: A robot walks 3 steps forward, 1 step back, then 2 steps forward. How far is it from the start?
questions.explanation: Forward 3 and back 1 leaves the robot 2 steps from the start. Then 2 more forward: 2 + 2 = 4 steps. A step back brings it closer to the start, so 6 is not right.
questions.hintText: Draw a line and move your finger along it for every command.

questions.question: IF it is your birthday, the program sings a song. Today is NOT your birthday. What does the program do?
questions.optionsString: It sings the song|It skips the song|It sings it twice|It sings it later
questions.explanation: The IF part is not true today, and there is no ELSE part. So the program skips the song and does nothing.
questions.hintText: Check whether the IF part is true today.

questions.question: A robot must draw a square. Its program is [REPEAT 3 TIMES: Draw a side, Turn]. What is the bug?
questions.optionsString: It must not turn|It must repeat 2 times|It must repeat 4 times|It must not draw
questions.explanation: A square has 4 sides, but the loop draws only 3. Change the 3 to a 4 and the square is complete.
questions.hintText: Count the sides of the shape. Then count how many sides the robot draws.

questions.question: A robot runs [REPEAT 3 TIMES: Jump 2 steps, Walk 1 step]. How many steps does it move in total?
questions.explanation: One round is 2 + 1 = 3 steps. The loop runs 3 rounds: 3 + 3 + 3 = 9 steps.
questions.hintText: First find the steps in one round. Then count all the rounds.

questions.question: A robot stands on square A1 of a chessboard. It moves 2 squares right and 1 square up. Where is it now?
questions.explanation: Two squares to the right of A are B and then C. One square up from row 1 is row 2. So the robot is on C2.
questions.hintText: Moving right changes the letter. Moving up changes the number.

questions.question: The score is 10. IF the score is more than 8, add 5. ELSE take away 5. What is the score now?
questions.explanation: Is 10 more than 8? Yes. So the IF part runs: 10 + 5 = 15. The ELSE part is skipped.
questions.hintText: Answer the IF question with yes or no first. Then do only that part.

questions.question: The box 'stars' holds 6. The program takes 2 out, then doubles the rest. How many are in the box now?
questions.explanation: Follow the steps in order: 6 − 2 = 4, then double 4 to get 8. If you double first, you get a different number, so order matters!
questions.hintText: Do the steps one at a time, in the order the program gives them.

questions.question: A game should end at 10 points. The code says: IF points = 5, say 'You win!'. What fixes the bug?
questions.optionsString: Delete the word IF|Change 'win' to 'lose'|Change 10 to 5|Change 5 to 10
questions.explanation: The code checks for the wrong number. The game should end at 10 points, so the 5 in the code must become 10.
questions.hintText: Compare the number the game needs with the number written in the code.

questions.question: REPEAT UNTIL the cup is full: add 1 spoon. The cup holds 5 spoons and already has 2. How many times does the loop run?
questions.explanation: The cup needs 5 − 2 = 3 more spoons. The loop adds 1 spoon each time, so it runs 3 times and then stops.
questions.hintText: How many spoons are still missing? The loop stops as soon as the cup is full.

questions.question: A number starts at 2. The program runs [REPEAT 3 TIMES: double the number]. What is the number at the end?
questions.explanation: Double it step by step: 2 becomes 4, 4 becomes 8, and 8 becomes 16. Each round uses the new number.
questions.hintText: Write down the new number after every round before you go on.

questions.question: A robot runs [REPEAT 4 TIMES: Forward 1 step, Turn left 90°]. Where does it end up?
questions.optionsString: 4 steps ahead of the start|2 steps left of the start|Back at the start|1 step behind the start
questions.explanation: Each round draws one side of a small square. After 4 sides and 4 turns the robot is back where it began, facing the same way.
questions.hintText: Draw the path on squared paper, one side at a time.
questions.acceptedAnswers: At the start|The start|Where it started

packs.title: Grandmaster Chess Endgames & Tactics
packs.subtitle: Interactive 2D FEN mating nets, forks, pins & sacrifices
packs.author: Kmito Chess Lab

questions.question: White to move: Deliver Opera Box Mate in 1 with the Rook on d1 supported by the Bishop on g5!
questions.explanation: Paul Morphy's Opera Game motif: 1. Rd8# mates the Black King because the g5 Bishop protects d8!
questions.hintText: Check along the open file where your Bishop stops the King from capturing the Rook.

questions.question: White to move: Execute Boden's Criss-Cross Bishop Checkmate in 1!
questions.explanation: 1. Ba6# checks along the a6-c8 diagonal while the f4 Bishop covers c7 and b8 and the Rook covers d7!
questions.hintText: The two Bishops work together: one gives check, the other seals the King's escape squares.

questions.question: White to move: Epaulette Mate! Black's King on e8 is flanked by its own two Rooks on d8 and f8. Deliver mate with the Queen!
questions.explanation: 1. Qe6# is Epaulette Mate! Black's own rooks on d8 and f8 act like shoulder pads blocking escape.
questions.hintText: Find the check that also covers both squares diagonally in front of the King.

questions.question: White to move: Anastasia's Mate! Knight on e7 controls g8 and g6; slide the Rook to the h-file for mate!
questions.explanation: 1. Rh3# completes Anastasia's Mate—the Knight on e7 takes away g8 and g6 while Black's g7 pawn blocks the King.
questions.hintText: Check along an open file: the Knight and the pawn already box in the King.

questions.question: What piece delivers the final checkmate in a classic Smothered Mate while the enemy King is surrounded by its own pieces?
questions.explanation: A Knight jumps over pieces to deliver checkmate to a trapped King boxed in by its own army.
questions.hintText: Only one piece can leap over the pieces crowding the King to give check.

questions.question: In a King and Pawn endgame, what critical concept involves placing your King directly opposite the enemy King with one square between them?
questions.explanation: The Opposition is a fundamental weapon to outflank the enemy King and escort your pawn to promotion.
questions.hintText: A battle over who has to move: the Kings face each other and one must give way.

questions.question: In the famous Lucena Rook endgame, what is the key tactical technique used to shield the King from vertical checks?
questions.optionsString: Underpromotion to Knight|Perpetual check|Building a bridge with the Rook (on the 4th rank)|Stalemate trick
questions.explanation: The 'Bridge Building' technique uses the Rook on the 4th rank (e.g. Rd4) to block checks and allow the pawn to promote.
questions.hintText: Your own Rook can step in front of the checks and act as a shield.

questions.question: How does the defending player draw a Rook and Pawn endgame in Philidor's 3rd-rank defense?
questions.optionsString: Keep the Rook on the 6th/3rd rank until the pawn advances, then check relentlessly from behind|Sacrifice the Rook immediately|Attack the enemy King from the side|Trade rooks immediately
questions.explanation: The defending Rook holds the 6th (or 3rd) rank cutting off the King. When the pawn pushes, the Rook checks from behind.
questions.hintText: Block the enemy King's path first; the checks only start once the pawn has advanced.

questions.question: What famous sacrifice involves offering a Bishop on h7 (or h2) with check to strip the castled King's shelter?
questions.optionsString: Damiano's Mate|Greek Gift Sacrifice (Bxh7+)|Blackburne's Mate|Legal's Mate
questions.explanation: The Greek Gift (Bxh7+) tears open the King's defense, followed by Ng5+ and Qh5.
questions.hintText: Think of the ancient story where a 'gift' let the enemy inside the walls.

questions.question: What does the German chess term 'Zugzwang' mean?
questions.optionsString: A rapid counter-attack|A perpetual sequence of checks|Having to move when every move is harmful|A sudden discovered checkmate
questions.explanation: Zugzwang is a situation where obligation to make a move leads to disadvantage or defeat.
questions.hintText: Think of a position where you wish you could simply pass the move.

questions.question: The 'Rule of the Square' allows a player to instantly determine what without calculation?
questions.optionsString: Whether castling is legally permitted|Whether a defending King can catch a passed pawn before it promotes|If a bishop can control two diagonals|How many rooks are active
questions.explanation: If the defending King can step inside the square of the passed pawn, it can catch and stop the pawn.
questions.hintText: Square drawn from the pawn to its promotion square.

questions.question: White pawns on a5, b5 and c5 face Black pawns on a7, b7 and c7, with White to move and both Kings too far away to interfere. Which move starts the winning breakthrough?
questions.optionsString: 1. a6|1. b6|1. c6|None: it is a draw
questions.explanation: 1. b6! forces a capture: after 1... axb6 2. c6! bxc6 3. a6, or 1... cxb6 2. a6! bxa6 3. c6, one White pawn runs through to queen. After 1. a6 or 1. c6 Black answers 1... b6 and keeps the pawns blocked.
questions.hintText: Give up one pawn so that a neighboring pawn becomes passed.

questions.question: When is an endgame with opposite-colored bishops notoriously prone to end in a draw?
questions.optionsString: Even when one side is down one or two pawns, because the defender establishes an impenetrable blockade on their color|Only when all pawns are traded|Never, opposite bishops always produce decisive wins|Only on move 50
questions.explanation: Opposite-colored bishops cannot challenge each other, enabling the defender to set up unbreakable color blockades.
questions.hintText: Each bishop stays on its own color: can they ever attack each other?

questions.question: What is a 'Windmill' tactic (such as in the famous Torre vs Lasker game)?
questions.optionsString: Spinning the rooks across all 4 corners|A repetitive sequence of discovered checks and regular checks using a Rook and Bishop to win multiple pieces|Promoting three pawns in consecutive turns|A perpetual queen sacrifice
questions.explanation: A windmill uses alternating discovered checks and direct checks with Rook and Bishop to vacuum up the opponent's pieces.
questions.hintText: Picture a windmill's sails turning: the same two pieces repeat a pattern again and again.

questions.question: What is the purpose of King triangulation in endgames?
questions.optionsString: To move across all three central files|To attack the enemy Queen from three directions|To lose a tempo and return to the original square, transferring the move to the opponent and putting them in zugzwang|To force stalemate
questions.explanation: Triangulation is a 3-move triangular King maneuver that wastes a tempo to hand the turn to the opponent.
questions.hintText: A short detour with the King can change who has to move.

questions.question: In Queen vs pawn-on-the-7th endings (defender's King near the pawn, enemy King far away), which pawns can still draw?
questions.optionsString: Knight and Central pawns (b, d, e, g pawns)|Rook pawns (a, h) and Bishop pawns (c, f)|Only the d-pawn|No pawn can draw against a Queen
questions.explanation: Rook pawns (a, h) and Bishop pawns (c, f) have stalemate resources in the corner, preventing the Queen from winning.
questions.hintText: Think about where the defender's King can hide in a corner to create stalemate.

questions.question: What was Richard Réti's genius concept in his 1921 study featuring a white King chasing two distant pawns?
questions.optionsString: The King walks a diagonal, making two threats at once|Sacrificing the King for a stalemate|Promoting to a bishop|Underpromoting to a knight
questions.explanation: Réti's diagonal King walk exploits Euclidean vs chessboard metric: walking diagonally closes distance to two separate goals simultaneously.
questions.hintText: Compare how many King moves each goal needs, then look for one path that serves both.

questions.question: White has a King, a light-squared Bishop and an h-pawn. What is the theoretical result if Black's King reaches h8?
questions.optionsString: White wins easily|It is a dead theoretical DRAW|Black wins|Loss on time
questions.explanation: The light-squared Bishop can never control the dark promotion square h8, so the defending King just shuffles between h8 and g8 and every attempt to dislodge it leads to stalemate.
questions.hintText: Compare the color of the Bishop's squares with the color of the corner square.

questions.question: What is the maximum number of moves required to checkmate with Bishop and Knight against a lone King from any position with best play?
questions.explanation: Under optimal play, Bishop and Knight mate can take up to 33 moves to drive the King into the corner matching the Bishop's color.
questions.hintText: The longest of the basic mates; a Knight 'W-maneuver' herds the King to the right corner.

questions.question: Which other endgame type are pure Knight and Pawn endgames most mathematically similar to?
questions.optionsString: Rook endgames|Pure King and Pawn endgames|Queen endgames|Bishop endgames
questions.explanation: Because Knights are short-range and cannot lose a tempo, pure Knight endgames closely mirror pure pawn endgames.
questions.hintText: Think of an ending with only short-range moves, where the fight is over key squares.

questions.question: What did Siegbert Tarrasch famously state regarding the placement of Rooks in endgames?
questions.optionsString: Rooks belong behind passed pawns — both behind your own to support them, and behind enemy pawns to halt them|Rooks should always stay on the starting rank|Rooks must capture bishops immediately|Rooks must avoid open files
questions.explanation: Tarrasch's rule: Place rooks behind passed pawns to maximize mobility as the pawn advances.
questions.hintText: Where does a Rook keep the most open lines while a passed pawn advances?

questions.question: Can a lone King and Rook force checkmate against a lone King?
questions.optionsString: No, it is a theoretical draw|Only if the King is trapped in the center|Yes, it is a basic fundamental checkmate|Only with pawns present
questions.explanation: King and Rook vs King is an elementary forced checkmate, pushing the King to any edge of the board.
questions.hintText: Recall the basic mates that every beginner learns first: what do they use?

questions.question: What is a 'Clearance Sacrifice' in grandmaster play?
questions.optionsString: Sacrificing a piece to clean the entire board|Sacrificing a piece specifically to vacate a square, file, or diagonal for a more deadly attacking piece|Resigning with grace|Trading queens in opening
questions.explanation: A clearance sacrifice frees a vital square or line (e.g. vacating f7 for a queen entry).
questions.hintText: Ask what the sacrificed piece was blocking.

questions.question: What is a 'Fortress' in chess endgames?
questions.optionsString: A defensive setup the stronger side cannot break down|Surrounding the King with 4 rooks|A double castling structure|A pawn chain stretching from a1 to h8
questions.explanation: A fortress is a theoretical draw where material superiority cannot breach the defensive perimeter.
questions.hintText: Think of a position where having extra material still cannot make progress.

questions.question: What is the tactical distinction between 'Deflection' and 'Decoy'?
questions.optionsString: They are exact synonyms with no distinction|Deflection forces a defending piece AWAY from a vital square, while Decoy lures an enemy piece ONTO a fatal square|Decoy is only used with pawns|Deflection only applies to the King
questions.explanation: Deflection removes a defender from duty; decoy pulls a piece onto a doomed square.
questions.hintText: To deflect is to turn aside; a decoy is a lure. Compare what each does to the piece.

questions.question: In Queen vs Rook endgame (Philidor position), what is the optimal result with best play?
questions.optionsString: Always a draw|Rook always wins|Queen wins by forcing zugzwang and winning the Rook|Loss by repetition
questions.explanation: Queen vs Rook is a forced win for the Queen, though technically demanding to execute without allowing stalemate.
questions.hintText: Compare the values of the two pieces, then ask whether the weaker side can hold.

questions.question: In the endgame, why does the King transform from a vulnerable target into an aggressive attacking piece?
questions.optionsString: Because check is no longer allowed in endgames|With few pieces remaining, the danger of checkmate drops dramatically, making the King an indispensable active fighter|The King gains the movement powers of a Queen|Pawns protect the King automatically
questions.explanation: As mating material decreases, the King must actively control central squares and assist passed pawns.
questions.hintText: Think about how many pieces are left to attack the King.

questions.question: What is a 'Zwischenzug' in tactical combinations?
questions.optionsString: A surprise move inserted before a recapture|Surrendering early|Offering a draw on move 1|A double pawn push
questions.explanation: A Zwischenzug inserts an intermediate threat (like check or counter-attack) before completing the expected line.
questions.hintText: Split the word: 'zwischen' + 'Zug'. Think about timing.

questions.question: What is an 'Isolated Pawn' and what is its primary endgame weakness?
questions.optionsString: A pawn with no enemy pawns ahead of it|No friendly pawns on adjacent files; only pieces can guard it|A pawn on the e-file|A pawn that moved three squares
questions.explanation: An isolated pawn cannot be defended by fellow pawns, becoming a chronic target in endgames.
questions.hintText: 'Isolated' means cut off: look at which pawns are missing next to it.

questions.question: What does it mean when a piece is 'Overloaded' in tactical calculations?
questions.optionsString: It weighs too much physically|It has moved more than 20 times|It has two defensive jobs and cannot do both|It is surrounded by 8 pieces
questions.explanation: An overloaded piece has multiple defensive duties; attacking one duty distracts it from the other.
questions.hintText: Count how many jobs the piece has to do at the same time.

questions.question: Why is the 'Bishop Pair' generally considered a significant long-term strategic advantage in open positions?
questions.optionsString: Because they can jump over pawns|Together they cover squares of both colours on open diagonals|They can castle together|They promote to two Queens simultaneously
questions.explanation: Two bishops complement each other, covering every square color on open boards where diagonals are clear.
questions.hintText: Think about the square color a single bishop can never reach.

questions.question: Why is a discovered check often so devastatingly powerful?
questions.optionsString: The moving piece can attack any target (even a Queen) while the unveiled piece simultaneously checks the King|It counts as two turns in a row|The opponent must surrender their Queen|The King cannot run away
questions.explanation: Because the King MUST respond to the check, the moving piece can capture material with complete impunity.
questions.hintText: The King must answer the check; what is the other piece free to do meanwhile?

questions.question: Why is a Rook invading the 7th rank (the 'Pig on the 7th') so prized in master play?
questions.optionsString: It promotes to Queen immediately|It attacks the enemy pawns and confines the King|It prevents all pawn moves|It doubles in value to 10 points
questions.explanation: The 7th rank is the home of vulnerable enemy pawns and clamps down on the enemy King.
questions.hintText: Ask what stands on the 7th rank at the start of a game, and where the enemy King sits.

questions.question: White to move: Black's King has no escape square behind its pawns. Find the back-rank mate in 1!
questions.explanation: 1. Rd8# is a back-rank mate: the Rook checks along the 8th rank and Black's own pawns on f7, g7 and h7 block every flight square.
questions.hintText: Your Rook can reach the rank where the King is boxed in.

questions.question: White to move: Black's King is walled in by its own Rook and pawns. Deliver the smothered mate in 1!
questions.explanation: 1. Nf7# is a smothered mate: the King on h8 is hemmed in by its own Rook on g8 and pawns on g7 and h7, and nothing can capture the Knight.
questions.hintText: Only one piece can give check to a King that is completely surrounded by its own men.

questions.question: White to move: Rook and Knight trap the King in the corner. Find the Arabian mate in 1!
questions.explanation: 1. Rh7# is the Arabian mate: the Knight on f6 protects the Rook and guards g8, while the Rook covers g7.
questions.hintText: The Knight already guards one flight square and can protect a piece next to the King.

questions.question: White to move: the pawn on g6 is a thorn in Black's castled position. Deliver Damiano's mate in 1!
questions.explanation: 1. Qh7# is Damiano's mate: the pawn on g6 protects the Queen and covers f7, and the Rook on f8 blocks its own King.
questions.hintText: Your advanced pawn can protect the Queen right next to the King.

questions.question: White to move: the Bishop on b2 rakes the long diagonal towards the black King. Find Mayet's mate in 1!
questions.explanation: 1. Rh8# is Mayet's mate: the Bishop on b2 protects the Rook on h8 and covers g7, and Black's own Rook and pawn block f8 and f7.
questions.hintText: Your Bishop can protect a piece that checks right beside the King.

questions.question: White to move: two Rooks on the 7th rank, the 'blind swine', finish the job. Find the mate in 1!
questions.explanation: 1. Rbg7# mates: the Rook on h7 protects its partner and covers h8, the Rook on g7 covers f7, and Black's own Rook blocks f8. After 1. Rhg7+ the King escapes to h8.
questions.hintText: Both Rooks can reach the same square: choose the one that leaves the other on guard.

questions.question: White to move: Black's own pawns take away two flight squares. Deliver the dovetail (Cozio's) mate in 1!
